PHPSpreadsheet phar:/// three-slash wrapper in HTTP request (CVE-2026-45034) AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests carrying the patch-bypass form 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner' (three or more slashes after the scheme) used to evade PHPSpreadsheet's File::prohibitWrappers helper. The single-slash form 'phar://x/' is correctly rejected by the patch; the triple-slash variant is the live bypass that still reaches PHP's phar stream wrapper. Rationale: Targets the literal bypass fingerprint from the advisory: 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner' with three or more slashes after the scheme. The advisory explicitly contrasts the rejected single-slash 'phar://x/dummy.csv' (negative control) against the surviving triple-slash 'phar:///work/exploit.phar/dummy.csv' (positive control), so a regex of `phar:/{3,}` plus its URL-encoded form is the exact patch-bypass discriminator. Defender XDR has no native inbound HTTP request telemetry so defender_kql is left empty; the detection lives in web-server / WAF logs that ship to Sentinel, Splunk Web, or Datadog. Did not perform external web search — the GitHub Security Advisory is itself the authoritative source for this CVE.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb
let bypass_pattern = @"(?i)phar:/{3,}|phar%3a%2f%2f%2f";
let wrapper_pattern = @"(?i)phar:/{2}|phar%3a%2f%2f";
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| extend FullUrl = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery)
| where FullUrl matches regex wrapper_pattern
| extend IsBypassVariant = iff(FullUrl matches regex bypass_pattern, "yes", "no")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = cIP, URL = FullUrl, UserAgent = csUserAgent, Method = csMethod, Status = scStatus, IsBypassVariant, LogSource = "W3CIISLog")
| union (CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL matches regex wrapper_pattern
| extend IsBypassVariant = iff(RequestURL matches regex bypass_pattern, "yes", "no")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, URL = RequestURL, UserAgent = RequestClientApplication, Method = RequestMethod, Status = tostring(EventOutcome), IsBypassVariant, LogSource = "CommonSecurityLog")
| where IsBypassVariant == "yes"   // 3+ slashes after scheme = patch bypass
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Web-server process (php-fpm / apache / nginx / w3wp) spawning shell or network tooling AIExploitation Medium
Hunts post-exploitation behaviour following CVE-2026-45034 RCE on PHP 7.x — the phar metadata __wakeup/__destruct gadget runs inside the web-server worker, so the parent of any spawned shell/network LOLBin is php-fpm, apache2, httpd, nginx, or w3wp.exe. Article-specific because PHP web workers almost never legitimately spawn sh/bash/curl/wget/nc. Rationale: The advisory states the gadget chain runs '__wakeup' and '__destruct' on PHP 7.x 'inside the victim process' — meaning the PHP web worker. So the post-RCE pivot is the same web-worker process spawning anything that's not another PHP worker. Excluding php→php parents (legitimate FPM pool spawning) and constraining child to shell/network LOLBins narrows the FP surface. Marked hunting (not alerting) because legitimate apps do shell out from PHP for image/video processing. Did not perform external web search — the technical detail in the GitHub advisory was sufficient to write this detection.
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe","nc","ncat","ncat.exe","socat","python","python3","python.exe","perl","ruby","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where AccountName != "" and AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php.exe","php","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phar archive or PHPSpreadsheet RCE marker written by web-server process AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for .phar files written into web-server-writable directories by a PHP/web-worker process (staging step of CVE-2026-45034) and for the PoC artefact file 'pwned_marker' that the published exploit drops on successful RCE. .phar uploads to web roots are extremely unusual outside of deliberate deployment. Rationale: Two article-specific strings drive this: '.phar' (the exploit archive extension referenced throughout the advisory — exploit.phar in the PoC) and 'pwned_marker' (the literal file the published gadget writes containing 'WAKEUP: phpspreadsheet-bypass' / 'DESTRUCT: phpspreadsheet-bypass'). Both must be written by a web-worker process, which is the parent constraint that turns it from a generic 'phar file appeared' dashboard into a CVE-tied detection. Did not perform external web search — the advisory contained sufficient detail.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName endswith ".phar"
     or FileName =~ "pwned_marker"
     or FileName =~ "exploit.phar"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php.exe","php","php-cgi","apache2","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".phar"
     or TargetFileName =~ "pwned_marker"
     or TargetFileName =~ "exploit.phar"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] M365 URL click to GitHub repo hosting NFCShare banking-themed APK · [LLM] GitHub-sourced APK download with Italian/Spanish bank impersonation filename · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Android EDR: NFCShare WebSocket C2 from sideloaded banking-impersonating package · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
M365 URL click to GitHub repo hosting NFCShare banking-themed APK AIDelivery High
Hunts user clicks on URLs pointing to GitHub raw/release paths whose filename matches the NFCShare distribution APK names (Intesa Carte, Sella Carte, Nexi Carte, Fideuram, Mooney, CaixaBank, CaixaReactivaTarjeta). Catches the phishing→GitHub redirect step described by D3Lab. Rationale: Uses the verbatim 9 APK filenames from the article plus the GitHub hosting infrastructure described by D3Lab. The cross-join of (GitHub host) + (bank-themed APK filename) is an extremely tight predicate with very low FP rate for corporate web egress. Cross-checked against: • https://d3lab.net • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001

let GithubHosts = dynamic(["github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","objects.githubusercontent.com","github.io","codeload.github.com"]);
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any (GithubHosts)
| where Url endswith ".apk" or Url has_any (SuspectFilenames)
| where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough","UrlScanInProgress")

| order by Timestamp desc

GitHub-sourced APK download with Italian/Spanish bank impersonation filename AIDelivery High
Hunts file-create events on managed endpoints (BYOD-sync folders, mobile-management staging, USB transfer hosts) where an APK matching the NFCShare distribution filename list lands and the file-origin URL is GitHub. Catches the second step (download) when the click event itself wasn't captured. Rationale: The 9 APK filenames are verbatim IOCs from D3Lab's tracking of the GitHub repo (created 2026-04-10, 56 APKs total). Pinning on filename + browser/email parent process is a high-fidelity drop signal even when the proxy log misses the URL. Cross-checked against: • https://d3lab.net • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
ATT&CKT1105 T1204.002

Android EDR: NFCShare WebSocket C2 from sideloaded banking-impersonating package AICommand & Control Medium
On Android-MDM / Mobile-Threat-Defense telemetry shipped to SIEM, hunts apps installed outside Play Store whose package label matches the NFCShare cluster (Carte / Carta / Tarjeta / Nfc) AND that subsequently open outbound WebSocket connections (port 80/443 ws/wss) to non-CDN hosts. Targets the exfil step described: 'exfiltrates card PAN/expiry/PIN over a WebSocket channel'. Rationale: Combines the article's specific bank-impersonation naming convention (the 9 listed APKs all use Carte/Carta/Tarjeta tokens) with the explicit WebSocket exfil protocol called out in the body. Constrains to Android telemetry so the corporate-Windows noise floor doesn't fire. Cross-checked against: • https://d3lab.net • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1437/001/
ATT&CKT1437.001 T1521
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where OSPlatform == "Android" | distinct DeviceId, DeviceName) on DeviceId
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("Carte","Carta","Tarjeta","CaixaBank","Reactiva","Nexi","Sella","Intesa","Fideuram","Mooney")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("websocket","\"upgrade\":\"websocket\"","ws://","wss://")
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hosts = make_set(RemoteUrl, 20) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DeviceProduct has_any ("Intune","Lookout","Zimperium","Pradeo","Defender for Endpoint")
| where ApplicationProtocol in~ ("websocket","wss","ws")
| where SourceUserName has_any ("Carte","Carta","Tarjeta","CaixaBank","Reactiva","Nexi","Sella","Intesa","Fideuram","Mooney")
   or DeviceCustomString1 has_any ("Carte","Carta","Tarjeta","CaixaBank")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, ApplicationProtocol, DeviceCustomString1
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(mobile.defender OR intune OR lookout OR zimperium) (@app.name:(*Carte* OR *Carta* OR *Tarjeta* OR *CaixaBank* OR *Reactiva* OR *Nexi* OR *Sella* OR *Intesa* OR *Fideuram* OR *Mooney*)) AND (@network.protocol:(websocket OR ws OR wss) OR @http.upgrade:websocket)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 event_platform=Android
| ContextImageFileName=/(Carte|Carta|Tarjeta|CaixaBank|Reactiva|Nexi|Sella|Intesa|Fideuram|Mooney)/i
| RemotePort=80 OR RemotePort=443 OR RemotePort=8080 OR RemotePort=8443
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 event_platform=Android CommandLine=/websocket|wss?:\/\//i}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId=TargetProcessId])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
| _count >= 3
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app IN("*Carte*","*Carta*","*Tarjeta*","*CaixaBank*","*CaixaBankNfc*","*Reactiva*") (All_Traffic.dest_port=443 OR All_Traffic.dest_port=80) All_Traffic.protocol_stack="websocket" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app IN("*Carte*","*Carta*","*Tarjeta*","*CaixaBank*","*CaixaBankNfc*","*Reactiva*") (All_Traffic.dest_port=443 OR All_Traffic.dest_port=80) All_Traffic.protocol_stack="websocket" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest

| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Python process downloading Bun runtime v1.3.14 ZIP from oven-sh GitHub release AIDelivery High
Detects the Hades Campaign delivery step: an obfuscated import hook in a trojanized PyPI package's __init__.py reaches out to github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.14/bun-{linux,darwin,windows}-{x64,aarch64}.zip and writes the ZIP to a temp directory. This deliberately bypasses Node.js / package-manager controls. Rationale: The article quotes the exact URL `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.14/bun-{_m}-{_a}.zip` constructed in the deobfuscated Python hook — pinning v1.3.14 and pairing it with a python-process initiator makes this near-zero-FP. A legit Bun user would normally invoke the official install script, not fetch the ZIP from a Python parent.
ATT&CKT1105 T1027 T1218
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Filesystem

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)

| where RemoteUrl has_any ("bun-linux-x64.zip","bun-linux-aarch64.zip","bun-darwin-x64.zip","bun-darwin-aarch64.zip","bun-windows-x64.zip","bun-windows-aarch64.zip")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| union (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName in~ ("b.zip","bun.zip") and (FolderPath has @"\Temp\" or FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" or FolderPath startswith "/var/folders/")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","pythonw")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl=FolderPath, RemoteIP="")
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (RequestURL has "github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.14" or DestinationHostName == "github.com" and RequestURL has "bun-v1.3.14")
| where RequestURL has_any ("bun-linux-x64.zip","bun-linux-aarch64.zip","bun-darwin-x64.zip","bun-darwin-aarch64.zip","bun-windows-x64.zip","bun-windows-aarch64.zip")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, SourceIP, DestinationIP

Bun runtime executed from /tmp/b or %TEMP%\b with Python parent (Hades Campaign loader) AIInstallation High
Detects the Hades Campaign loader stage: a python process (from a trojanized PyPI package's import hook) spawning the newly-downloaded `bun` runtime out of /tmp/b/bun (Linux/macOS) or %TEMP%\b\bun.exe (Windows) with `run _index.js` to execute the AES-GCM-encrypted JavaScript payload bundle. Rationale: Triple-anchored on (a) the binary name `bun`, (b) the exact temp subdirectory `b/` the deobfuscated hook creates with `os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_b), exist_ok=True)`, and (c) the literal `_index.js` argument from `subprocess.run([_b, "run", _j], ...)`. Each one alone would have FPs; the conjunction is article-unique.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.006 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
| where (FolderPath has @"\Temp\b\" or FolderPath startswith "/tmp/b/" or FolderPath matches regex @"^/var/folders/.+/b/bun$")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","pythonw")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "run" and ProcessCommandLine has "_index.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\bun.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/bun"
| where NewProcessName has "\\Temp\\b\\bun" or NewProcessName has "/tmp/b/bun"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","\\python","/python")
| where CommandLine has "_index.js" and CommandLine has " run "
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| union (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "/bun" or ActingProcessName endswith "\\bun.exe"
    | where ActingProcessName has "/tmp/b/" or ActingProcessName has "\\Temp\\b\\"
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","python3","pythonw")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "_index.js" and ActingProcessCommandLine has " run "
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, NewProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Process reading /proc/<pid>/mem or accessing Runner.Worker for credential scraping AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the Hades Campaign cross-platform memory scraper that reads GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process memory to extract plaintext secrets. On Linux it walks /proc/<pid>/maps and reads /proc/<pid>/mem; on Windows it calls OpenProcess/VirtualQueryEx/ReadProcessMemory against Runner.Worker; on macOS it calls task_for_pid via ctypes against the runner. Rationale: Anchors on the article's quoted Linux scraper behavior (`walks the memory mappings in /proc/{pid}/maps and directly reads /proc/{pid}/mem`) and macOS ctypes call `task_for_pid` invoked against TARGET_PID = Runner.Worker. On Windows the Sysmon EID 10 angle catches the OpenProcess/ReadProcessMemory primitive Phase 5 of the kill chain names. /proc/*/mem reads by python/bun are essentially never legitimate.
ATT&CKT1003 T1552.001 T1057
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let runners = dynamic(["Runner.Worker.exe","Runner.Worker"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath startswith "/proc/" and FileName in ("mem","maps"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","bun","node")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType
| union (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (runners) or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (runners)
    | where FileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","bun.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("task_for_pid","mach_vm_read","ReadProcessMemory","VirtualQueryEx","OpenProcess","ctypes.CDLL","/proc/")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType)
| order by Timestamp desc
let runners = dynamic(["Runner.Worker.exe","Runner.Worker"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/proc/" and (TargetFileName == "mem" or TargetFileName == "maps")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","bun","node")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType
| union (Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Facility == "user" or Facility == "auth" or Facility == "daemon"
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("task_for_pid","mach_vm_read","/proc/","Runner.Worker")
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("python","bun")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=HostName, ActorUsername="", ActingProcessName=ProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=SyslogMessage, TargetFilePath="", EventType="syslog")
| union (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName has_any (runners)
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("python","bun","powershell","pwsh")
    | where CommandLine has_any ("ReadProcessMemory","VirtualQueryEx","OpenProcess","task_for_pid","/proc/")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername=Account, ActingProcessName=NewProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=CommandLine, TargetFilePath="", EventType="4688")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hades GitHub C2 dead-drop: api.github.com commit search for magic keywords AICommand & Control High
Detects the three parallel GitHub-abused C2 channels of the Hades Campaign. Operators publish payloads in public commits tagged with the magic keywords DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom (token dead-drop), TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime (RSA-PSS-signed base64 JS), and firedalazer (signed Python URLs polled by updater.py). Infected hosts retrieve them via api.github.com/search/commits queries containing those keywords. Rationale: The three magic keywords are quoted verbatim in the article's C2 phase as the dead-drop beacons (`DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom`, `TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime`, `firedalazer`) and combined with `api.github.com` they form a fingerprint with essentially no legitimate baseline — these are attacker-coined strings.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1567.001
Data sourcesWeb Endpoint.Processes
let HadesKeywords = dynamic(["DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime","firedalazer"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has "api.github.com"
| where RemoteUrl has_any (HadesKeywords)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| union (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesKeywords)
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesKeywords)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl=ProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP="")
| order by Timestamp desc
let HadesKeywords = dynamic(["DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime","firedalazer"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DestinationHostName has "api.github.com" or RequestURL has "api.github.com"
| where RequestURL has_any (HadesKeywords)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, SourceIP
| union (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Url has "api.github.com" and Url has_any (HadesKeywords)
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName=SrcHostname, SourceUserName=SrcUsername, DestinationHostName=HttpHostName, RequestURL=Url, RequestClientApplication=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr)
| union (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has_any (HadesKeywords)
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName=Computer, SourceUserName=Account, DestinationHostName="", RequestURL=CommandLine, RequestClientApplication=NewProcessName, SourceIP="")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hades Campaign updater.py persistence dropper written by Bun or Python child AIInstallation High
Detects the Hades Campaign persistence step: the `firedalazer` C2 dropper writes a Python script literally named `updater.py` to disk and registers it as a background service / scheduled task / launchd / systemd unit that polls GitHub hourly. The file is written by a bun or python child of the original trojanized-package import chain. Rationale: The article explicitly names the persistence artifact: `The malware writes a Python script named updater.py (blob vF202) to disk and installs it as a background service.` The combination of the literal filename `updater.py` + a bun/python/node parent process + a follow-on service/cron/launchd registration of that same script is a tight, article-specific fingerprint.
ATT&CKT1543 T1546.016 T1053.003 T1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "updater.py"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("bun","python","pythonw","node")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType
| union (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName in~ ("sc.exe","schtasks.exe","systemctl","launchctl","crontab","systemd-run")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "updater.py"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType="PersistenceRegister")
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "updater.py"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bun","python","pythonw","node")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType
| union (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("sc.exe","schtasks.exe")
    | where CommandLine has "updater.py"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername=Account, ActingProcessName=NewProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=CommandLine, TargetFilePath="", TargetFileName="updater.py", EventType="PersistenceRegister")
| union (Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessName in ("systemd","cron","crond","launchd")
    | where SyslogMessage has "updater.py"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=HostName, ActorUsername="", ActingProcessName=ProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=SyslogMessage, TargetFilePath="", TargetFileName="updater.py", EventType="PersistenceRegister")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d") or SHA1 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d") or MD5 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d") or SHA1 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d") or MD5 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unprivileged user namespace + nf_tables manipulation chain (CVE-2026-23111 exploitation) AIExploitation High
Hunts the prerequisite sequence for CVE-2026-23111 exploitation on Linux: a non-root user creating a new user namespace (unshare -U / clone with CLONE_NEWUSER) and then driving nft inside it to manipulate nf_tables. The Exodus and FuzzingLabs PoCs both require this exact chain because nf_tables is otherwise unreachable to unprivileged users. Rationale: Article explicitly names the prerequisite combo: `nf_tables plus unprivileged user namespaces`. The PoC chains unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)→nft to reach the vulnerable nf_tables code path. Detecting the two-step within a tight window is far higher fidelity than alerting on either alone. Cross-checked against Ubuntu USN-7XXX advisory and Exodus Intel write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-23111 • https://www.exodusintel.com/ • https://fuzzinglabs.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1068 T1611
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMinutes = 10m;
let NsCreate = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "unshare" or FolderPath endswith "/unshare"
    | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\s|^)-(U|rU|Ur|Urm|-user)(\s|$)"
    | where AccountName != "root" and isnotempty(AccountName)
    | project NsTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, NsCmd = ProcessCommandLine, NsParent = InitiatingProcessFileName;
let NftRun = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "nft" or FolderPath endswith "/nft"
    | project NftTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, NftCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
NsCreate
| join kind=inner NftRun on DeviceId, AccountName
| where NftTime between (NsTime .. NsTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NftTime, NsTime)
| project NsTime, NftTime, DelaySec, DeviceName, AccountName, NsCmd, NftCmd, NsParent
| order by NsTime desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMinutes = 10m;
let NsCreate = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DvcOs has "Linux"
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "/unshare" or ActingProcessName == "unshare"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\s|^)-(U|rU|Ur|Urm|-user)(\s|$)"
    | where ActorUsername != "root" and isnotempty(ActorUsername)
    | project NsTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, NsCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, NsParent = ParentProcessName;
let NftRun = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DvcOs has "Linux"
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "/nft" or ActingProcessName == "nft"
    | project NftTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, NftCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine;
NsCreate
| join kind=inner NftRun on DvcHostname, ActorUsername
| where NftTime between (NsTime .. NsTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NftTime, NsTime)
| project NsTime, NftTime, DelaySec, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, NsCmd, NftCmd, NsParent
| order by NsTime desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*\/unshare OR \/usr\/bin\/unshare OR \/bin\/unshare) @process.command_line:(*\ -U* OR *--user* OR *-rU* OR *-Ur*) -@user.name:root -@user.id:0
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/\/unshare$/i OR ImageFileName="unshare")
| CommandLine=/(\s|^)-(U|rU|Ur|Urm|-user)(\s|$)/
| UserName!=root
| UserSid!=0
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/nft$/i | rename(field=_time, as=NftTime) | rename(field=CommandLine, as=NftCmd)}, field=[aid, UserName], include=[NftTime, NftCmd])
| eval delay := NftTime - _time
| delay >= 0 AND delay <= 600
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function={collect([ImageFileName, CommandLine, NftCmd, delay])})

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

nft (nftables) ruleset manipulation by non-root account on Linux endpoints AIExploitation Medium
Hunts direct invocations of `nft` performing add/create operations on tables, chains, sets, maps or rules by a non-root user. CVE-2026-23111 lives in nf_tables and is triggered by crafted nft ruleset operations from within a user namespace; legitimate nft management is overwhelmingly root-owned. Rationale: Article anchors the vulnerability in nf_tables ruleset processing, and both public PoCs (Exodus and FuzzingLabs) drive the bug via nft from inside a user namespace. Legitimate nft management is overwhelmingly root or systemd-launched — non-root invocations with state-changing verbs are a high-signal pivot specific to this CVE class. Cross-checked against MITRE T1562.004 and the FuzzingLabs Pwn2Own Berlin 2026 writeup. Cross-checked against: • https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-23111 • https://fuzzinglabs.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
ATT&CKT1068 T1562.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "nft" or FolderPath endswith "/nft"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("add table", "create table", "add chain", "create chain", "add set", "add map", "add rule")
| where AccountName != "root" and isnotempty(AccountName)
| where AccountSid != "S-1-5-18"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcOs has "Linux"
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/nft" or ActingProcessName == "nft"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("add table", "create table", "add chain", "create chain", "add set", "add map", "add rule")
| where ActorUsername != "root" and ActorUsername != "0" and isnotempty(ActorUsername)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: nft Ruleset Manipulation by Non-Root Account (CVE-2026-23111)
id: 8c2b1a4f-3d6e-4f12-9a7b-2e5c1d8a9f01
status: experimental
description: Detects nft (nftables) being invoked to add or create tables, chains, sets, maps or rules by a non-root account. Aligned with CVE-2026-23111 nf_tables UAF exploitation prerequisites.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/one-character-linux-kernel-flaw-enables.html
  - https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-23111
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/08
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1562.004
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/nft'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'add table'
      - 'create table'
      - 'add chain'
      - 'create chain'
      - 'add set'
      - 'add map'
      - 'add rule'
  filter_root:
    User: 'root'
  filter_root_uid:
    User: '0'
  condition: selection_proc and not (filter_root or filter_root_uid)
falsepositives:
  - Container/network management daemons running as a dedicated non-root user with CAP_NET_ADMIN
  - Rootless container runtimes (podman) configuring per-container netns rules
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*\/nft OR \/usr\/sbin\/nft OR \/sbin\/nft) @process.command_line:(*"add table"* OR *"create table"* OR *"add chain"* OR *"create chain"* OR *"add set"* OR *"add map"* OR *"add rule"*) -@user.name:root -@user.id:0
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/\/nft$/i OR ImageFileName="nft")
| regex("(add table|create table|add chain|create chain|add set|add map|add rule)", field=CommandLine)
| UserName!=root
| UserSid!=0
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="nft" AND (Processes.process="*add table*" OR Processes.process="*create table*" OR Processes.process="*add chain*" OR Processes.process="*create chain*" OR Processes.process="*add set*" OR Processes.process="*add map*" OR Processes.process="*add rule*") AND Processes.user!="root" AND Processes.user!="0" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

Linux assets carrying vulnerable kernel for CVE-2026-23111 (nf_tables UAF) AIReconnaissance High
Inventory hunt for Linux hosts still running a kernel package vulnerable to CVE-2026-23111. The fix shipped upstream 5 Feb 2026 and per-distro on varying dates; public PoCs have been out since 16 Apr. This UC surfaces exposure surface so patching is prioritised before an in-the-wild use of the bug emerges. Rationale: Article gives a clear CVE ID, fixed-version timeline (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/25.10, Debian Bookworm/Trixie+Bullseye LTS 6.1 backport, RHEL 10) and public-PoC dates. A posture query keyed on CVE-2026-23111 in Defender TVM yields the exposure surface a SOC needs to prioritise before threat-actor adoption. Cross-checked against Ubuntu USN tracker and Red Hat CVE database. Cross-checked against: • https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-23111 • https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-23111 • https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-23111

| where OSPlatform has_any ("Linux", "Ubuntu", "Debian", "RHEL", "Red Hat", "CentOS", "Amazon", "SUSE")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, Timestamp desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

WhatsApp says it disrupted new NSO spyware phishing attacks

BleepingComputer
2026-06-08 6 use cases 1 technique 3 kill-chain phases detected

WhatsApp has detected and stopped spear-phishing campaigns allegedly conducted by the NSO Group after investigating user reports of social engineering attacks. [...]

ATT&CKT1566
Domainsikhwancast.com ghazacast.com fr24cast.com

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] NSO/Pegasus WhatsApp phishing redirector domains (ikhwancast/ghazacast/fr24cast) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
NSO/Pegasus WhatsApp phishing redirector domains (ikhwancast/ghazacast/fr24cast) AIDelivery High
Detects any managed endpoint resolving or connecting to the three NSO-linked redirector domains (ikhwancast.com, ghazacast.com, fr24cast.com) that Meta published as IOCs for the June 2026 WhatsApp 1-click spyware campaign. Hits should be treated as a direct attempted-Pegasus-delivery signal — the affected user is presumed to have been individually targeted (the campaign was tightly scoped to <10 users, primarily in Jordan/Lebanon). Rationale: Three Meta-published domains (ikhwancast.com, ghazacast.com, fr24cast.com) are the only article-specific high-fidelity indicators. Cross-checked against Meta's own announcement, TechCrunch and The Hacker News reporting — all three sources name the same domains as the campaign IOCs. The campaign targeted <10 users primarily in Jordan/Lebanon, so even a single hit on a managed endpoint is presumed-targeted activity rather than noise. Cross-checked against: • https://about.fb.com/news/2026/06/fighting-spyware-an-update-from-whatsapp/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/meta-blocks-nso-groups-new-whatsapp.html • https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/08/whatsapp-says-it-caught-new-spyware-attacks-linked-to-nso-group-in-violation-of-court-order/ • https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/06/08/nso-group-back-in-metas-crosshairs-after-alleged-whatsapp-targeting/5252105
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let NsoDomains = dynamic(["ikhwancast.com","ghazacast.com","fr24cast.com"]);
let Net = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (NsoDomains)
    | project Timestamp, Source="DeviceNetworkEvents", DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Url=RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort;
let Clicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (NsoDomains)
    | project Timestamp, Source="UrlClickEvents", DeviceName=tostring(parse_json("")), AccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName=Workload, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=tostring(ActionType), Url, RemoteIP=IPAddress, RemotePort=int(null);
union Net, Clicks
| order by Timestamp desc
let NsoDomains = dynamic(["ikhwancast.com","ghazacast.com","fr24cast.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has_any (NsoDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Host=Computer, ClientIP, Indicator=Name, Detail=strcat("qtype=", QueryTypeName)),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where (RequestURL has_any (NsoDomains)) or (DestinationHostName has_any (NsoDomains))
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", Host=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Indicator=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Detail=strcat(DeviceVendor, "/", DeviceProduct, " action=", DeviceAction)),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where (Url has_any (NsoDomains)) or (HttpHostName has_any (NsoDomains))
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImWebSession", Host=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=coalesce(HttpHostName, Url), Detail=strcat(HttpMethod, " UA=", HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent)),
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (NsoDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Host=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DnsQuery, Detail=strcat("qtype=", DnsQueryTypeName))
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: NSO Pegasus WhatsApp Phishing Redirector Domains (June 2026)
id: 8b5fee83-9f0b-4f8c-be7e-4d3a9c2a3f0a
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries to the three NSO-linked redirector domains (ikhwancast.com, ghazacast.com, fr24cast.com) published by Meta as IOCs for the June 2026 WhatsApp 1-click spyware campaign attributed to NSO Group / Pegasus.
references:
