  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/meta-blocks-nso-groups-new-whatsapp.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Check Point Remote Access VPN inbound auth from CVE-2026-50751 actor VPS IPs AIExploitation High
Detects inbound IKE/IPSec authentication or SSL VPN login attempts to Check Point Remote Access / Mobile Access gateways from the eight VPS IPs Check Point published as the CVE-2026-50751 / Qilin-affiliate infrastructure. Article-specific because it pivots on the published IOC IP set and on IKEv1 / Mobile Access ports. Rationale: Pivots on the eight VPS IPs Check Point published (article body) and the IKEv1 / Mobile Access ports the bypass requires. Cross-checked with Check Point's own blog and BleepingComputer write-up confirming the same IP set and hosting providers (Vultr, Shock Hosting, Kaupo Cloud HK). Cross-checked against: • https://blog.checkpoint.com/security/check-point-releases-important-hotfix-for-vulnerabilities-in-deprecated-ikev1-vpn-protocol/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/check-point-links-vpn-zero-day-attacks-to-qilin-ransomware-gang/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/06/08/check-point-cve-2026-50751-qilin-ransomware/
ATT&CKT1190 T1133

| where RemoteIP in ("45.77.149.152","209.182.225.136","38.60.157.139","162.33.177.101","45.76.26.42","144.208.127.155","38.54.88.201","38.54.107.167")
| where LocalPort in (500, 4500, 443)

CommonSecurityLog

title: Check Point VPN Inbound Connection From CVE-2026-50751 Qilin Actor Infrastructure
id: 5b2e6c2a-4f1f-4f73-9b2e-7b04a51a9f01
description: Inbound IKE/IPSec/SSL-VPN connection to a Check Point gateway from one of the eight VPS IPs published by Check Point as the CVE-2026-50751 exploit infrastructure linked to a Qilin ransomware affiliate.
references:
  - https://blog.checkpoint.com/security/check-point-releases-important-hotfix-for-vulnerabilities-in-deprecated-ikev1-vpn-protocol/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/critical-check-point-vpn-flaw-exploited.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/08
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1133

  category: firewall
  product: checkpoint
detection:
  selection:
    src_ip:
      - '45.77.149.152'
      - '209.182.225.136'
      - '38.60.157.139'
      - '162.33.177.101'
      - '45.76.26.42'
      - '144.208.127.155'
      - '38.54.88.201'
      - '38.54.107.167'
    dst_port:
      - 500
      - 4500
      - 443
  condition: selection
level: high
(source:checkpoint OR source:checkpoint.firewall OR source:syslog) (@network.client.ip:("45.77.149.152" OR "209.182.225.136" OR "38.60.157.139" OR "162.33.177.101" OR "45.76.26.42" OR "144.208.127.155" OR "38.54.88.201" OR "38.54.107.167") OR @network.destination.ip:("45.77.149.152" OR "209.182.225.136" OR "38.60.157.139" OR "162.33.177.101" OR "45.76.26.42" OR "144.208.127.155" OR "38.54.88.201" OR "38.54.107.167")) @network.destination.port:(500 OR 4500 OR 443)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ConnectionDirection=1
| RemoteAddressIP4=/^(45\.77\.149\.152|209\.182\.225\.136|38\.60\.157\.139|162\.33\.177\.101|45\.76\.26\.42|144\.208\.127\.155|38\.54\.88\.201|38\.54\.107\.167)$/
| LocalPort=/^(500|4500|443)$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, LocalPort], function=count())
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs   (point at the VPC hosting Check Point CloudGuard / VPN concentrator ENIs)
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, srcPort, dstAddr, dstPort, protocol, action, bytes
| filter srcAddr in ["45.77.149.152","209.182.225.136","38.60.157.139","162.33.177.101","45.76.26.42","144.208.127.155","38.54.88.201","38.54.107.167"]
      and dstPort in [500, 4500, 443]
      and action = "ACCEPT"
| sort @timestamp desc

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(dest) as gateway values(dest_port) as dest_port values(action) as action from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (sourcetype IN ("opsec","cp_log","checkpoint:firewall","checkpoint:vpn") OR All_Traffic.dest_port IN (500,4500,443) AND All_Traffic.action!="blocked") AND All_Traffic.src IN ("45.77.149.152","209.182.225.136","38.60.157.139","162.33.177.101","45.76.26.42","144.208.127.155","38.54.88.201","38.54.107.167") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.action | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | eval firstSeen=strftime(firstSeen,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"), lastSeen=strftime(lastSeen,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
Qilin Linux ransomware ELF payload (CVE-2026-50751 campaign) — known MD5 file event AIInstallation High
Detects file write, file open, or process execution of a Linux ELF whose MD5 matches one of the two payloads Check Point attributed to the post-VPN-bypass Qilin affiliate stage. Specific to this article because it ships the two MD5 hashes the vendor published. Rationale: Both MD5s are taken verbatim from the article's IOC block and corroborated by Check Point's own advisory (linked to Qilin Linux ELF binaries per the BleepingComputer write-up). High-fidelity — file hashes do not collide with benign software in practice. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.checkpoint.com/security/check-point-releases-important-hotfix-for-vulnerabilities-in-deprecated-ikev1-vpn-protocol/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/check-point-links-vpn-zero-day-attacks-to-qilin-ransomware-gang/
ATT&CKT1486 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let qilinHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689","51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(45d)
    | where MD5 in (qilinHashes)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="FileEvent", ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName),
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(45d)
    | where MD5 in (qilinHashes)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="ProcessEvent", ActionType="ProcessCreated", FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName)
| order by Timestamp asc
let qilinHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689","51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
| where TargetFileMD5 in (qilinHashes) or Hash in (qilinHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileMD5, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated asc

Rclone exfiltration from Check Point VPN gateway or post-bypass internal host AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects rclone execution to a remote cloud target from a host that recently terminated a Remote Access VPN session — the exfiltration tradecraft Check Point and BleepingComputer attribute to this Qilin affiliate following CVE-2026-50751. Article-specific because it pairs rclone (named in the external advisories) with the Check Point campaign window. Rationale: Article body names rclone abuse and ELF download from actor-controlled infra in the post-exploit phase; cross-checked with Check Point's blog and BleepingComputer's write-up which both explicitly call out rclone. The combination of rclone binary + transfer verb + cloud remote prefix is the published tradecraft. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.checkpoint.com/security/check-point-releases-important-hotfix-for-vulnerabilities-in-deprecated-ikev1-vpn-protocol/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/check-point-links-vpn-zero-day-attacks-to-qilin-ransomware-gang/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(45d)
| where FileName =~ "rclone" or FileName =~ "rclone.exe" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\brclone\b"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("copy","sync","move","copyto","moveto","cat")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s(mega|s3|b2|drive|dropbox|onedrive|pcloud|box|gcs|azureblob|webdav|sftp|ftp|remote):"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/|\\)rclone(\.exe)?$" or TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/|\\)rclone(\.exe)?$" or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\brclone\b"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("copy","sync","move","copyto","moveto","cat")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s(mega|s3|b2|drive|dropbox|onedrive|pcloud|box|gcs|azureblob|webdav|sftp|ftp|remote):"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Internal host outbound to CVE-2026-50751 Qilin actor IPs (post-bypass C2 / staging) AICommand & Control High
Detects outbound network connections from any internal host to the eight VPS IPs Check Point published — i.e. an inside-out beacon or staging callback after the VPN gateway was compromised. Article-specific because the IPs are the exact post-exploit infrastructure named in the IOC block. Rationale: All eight IPs taken directly from the article IOC block; the BleepingComputer and Check Point sources confirm these are the actor-controlled VPS nodes used for both the bypass and post-exploit ELF staging. Outbound to a known-bad IP set is one of the cleanest signal shapes in detection engineering. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.checkpoint.com/security/check-point-releases-important-hotfix-for-vulnerabilities-in-deprecated-ikev1-vpn-protocol/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/check-point-links-vpn-zero-day-attacks-to-qilin-ransomware-gang/ • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/06/08/attackers-had-month-long-head-start-on-patched-check-point-vpn-zero-day/5252438

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.

DeviceProcessEvents

| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"

logsource:

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |

    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic

references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication

      AND Authentication.signature IN (

        "Add app role assignment grant to user",

    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Gogs Merge() argument injection — git rebase invoked with --exec= flag AIExploitation High
Detects exploitation of the Gogs Merge() argument-injection zero-day (GHSA-qf6p-p7ww-cwr9, fixed in 0.14.3). The vulnerable code path passes a PR branch name beginning with -- directly to `git rebase`; supplying a branch named `--exec=<cmd>` causes git rebase to shell-exec the attacker command. This rule alerts whenever the gogs process spawns git with a rebase invocation that carries `--exec=` — there is no legitimate reason for the gogs daemon to ever run `git rebase --exec=`. Rationale: Anchored on the exact exploit primitive disclosed in the Rapid7 advisory and confirmed by Gogs PR #8301: an attacker-controlled branch name (`--exec=<cmd>`) reaches `git rebase` via Merge(). The cmdline pair `rebase` + `--exec=` under a `gogs` parent is uniquely diagnostic — the fixed code rejects leading-`-` branches and adds `--end-of-options`, so a patched server will not produce this pattern at all. Cross-checked: Rapid7 blog, BleepingComputer, Gogs PR #8301 / GHSA-qf6p-p7ww-cwr9. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ve-authenticated-rce-via-argument-injection-gogs-unfixed/ • https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8301 • https://www.rapid7.com/db/vulnerabilities/gogs-git-rebase-argument-injection/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/critical-gogs-rce-vulnerability-lets.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Gogs Merge() argument injection — GHSA-qf6p-p7ww-cwr9 / fixed in PR #8301
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("gogs","gogs.exe")
      or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("gogs","gogs.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("git","git.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "rebase"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--exec="
     or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s--exec(=|\s)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          FolderPath, SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// Gogs Merge() argument injection — gogs spawns `git rebase --exec=`
let Window = 7d;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
  | where ActingProcessName has "gogs" or ParentProcessName has "gogs"
  | where TargetProcessName has "git"
  | where TargetProcessCommandLine has "rebase" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--exec="
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
            ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
),
(
  SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("gogs","gogs.exe")
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\git.exe","/git")
  | where CommandLine has "rebase" and CommandLine has "--exec="
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ActorUsername=SubjectUserName,
            ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName=NewProcessName,
            TargetProcessName=NewProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine=CommandLine
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Gogs daemon ancestry spawns shell / downloader (post-arg-injection RCE) AIInstallation Medium
Defense-in-depth hunt for the post-exploitation stage of the Gogs Merge() argument-injection bug. After `git rebase --exec=<cmd>` runs, `<cmd>` is shell-exec'd as a descendant of the gogs daemon — so the diagnostic shape is gogs → git → (sh|bash|curl|wget|python|nc|powershell) with a payload-flavoured cmdline. Tuned to suppress legitimate Gogs server-side git hooks (pre-receive / post-receive / post-update). Rationale: Targets the second-order signal of the Gogs Merge() RCE: once `git rebase --exec=<cmd>` succeeds, `<cmd>` is shell-spawned with gogs as a near-ancestor. The downloader/reverse-shell regex (DownloadString, /dev/tcp/, bash -i, curl/wget, base64 -d) keeps signal high; the explicit exclusion of `hooks/(pre|post)-receive` paths removes the dominant legitimate noise source (gogs runs server-side git hooks as the gogs user). Cross-checked Rapid7 advisory plus PR #8301 patch which inserts `--end-of-options` confirming exec is the abuse target. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ve-authenticated-rce-via-argument-injection-gogs-unfixed/ • https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8301 • https://www.rapid7.com/db/vulnerabilities/gogs-git-rebase-argument-injection/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Post-arg-injection shell / downloader spawned by Gogs ancestry
let GogsAncestor = dynamic(["gogs","gogs.exe"]);
let SuspiciousChildren = dynamic([
  "sh","bash","dash","zsh","ash","ksh",
  "cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe",
  "curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe",
  "python","python3","perl","ruby","php",
  "nc","ncat","ncat.exe","socat",
  "certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (GogsAncestor)
      or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (GogsAncestor)
| where FileName in~ (SuspiciousChildren)
// Discriminate from legit server-side git hooks (pre-receive / post-receive / post-update)
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(curl\s|wget\s|/dev/tcp/|bash\s+-i|nc\s+-[^\s]*[el]|chmod\s+\+x|/tmp/|/dev/shm/|certutil\s+-(urlcache|decode)|powershell\s+-(e|nop|w hidden)|IEX\s|DownloadString|base64\s+-d)"
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("hooks/pre-receive","hooks/post-receive","hooks/update","hooks/post-update"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc

Internet-facing Gogs instances on pre-0.14.3 (CVE-pending Merge() injection) AIReconnaissance High
Inventory hunt for Gogs servers running a version vulnerable to the Merge() argument-injection zero-day disclosed by Rapid7 — all releases up to and including 0.14.2 and any 0.15.0+dev build. Returns one row per device with vulnerable version, prioritised by whether the host is Internet-facing (Shadowserver tracks ~2,300 exposed Gogs servers globally; ~1,800 in Asia, ~300 in Europe). Rationale: Article explicitly names the vulnerable bracket — all releases up to and including 0.14.2 and 0.15.0+dev, fixed in 0.14.3. Confirmed via the Rapid7 vulnerability database entry and Gogs PR #8301. Joining DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing surfaces the assets that match Shadowserver's exposed-Gogs cohort (2,300 instances). This is a one-shot hunt to drive emergency patching, not a recurring alert. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/db/vulnerabilities/gogs-git-rebase-argument-injection/ • https://www.runzero.com/blog/gogs/ • https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8301
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Internet-facing Gogs instances on vulnerable versions (≤ 0.14.2, 0.15.0+dev)
let GogsAssets = DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
  | where SoftwareName =~ "gogs" or (SoftwareVendor =~ "gogs" and SoftwareName has "gogs")
  | extend VerNoMeta = tostring(split(SoftwareVersion, "+")[0])
  | extend Parts = split(VerNoMeta, ".")
  | extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Patch = toint(Parts[2])
  | extend IsDevBuild = SoftwareVersion has "+dev"
  | where Major == 0
        and ((Minor < 14)
          or (Minor == 14 and Patch <= 2)
          or (Minor == 15 and IsDevBuild));
GogsAssets
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform, OSVersion) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing,
          SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
// Internet-facing Gogs instances on vulnerable versions — Sentinel (DeviceTvm* unified table)
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where SoftwareName =~ "gogs" or (SoftwareVendor =~ "gogs" and SoftwareName has "gogs")
| extend VerNoMeta = tostring(split(SoftwareVersion, "+")[0])
| extend Parts = split(VerNoMeta, ".")
| extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Patch = toint(Parts[2])
| extend IsDevBuild = SoftwareVersion has "+dev"
| where Major == 0
      and ((Minor < 14)
        or (Minor == 14 and Patch <= 2)
        or (Minor == 15 and IsDevBuild))
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing,
          SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion
| order by IsInternetFacing desc
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/[\\\/]gogs(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=[count(), min(_time, as=firstSeen), max(_time, as=lastSeen), collect([CommandLine, ImageFileName])])
// Pair with FDR ManagedAssets / FalconSpotlight to filter to versions <= 0.14.2 or 0.15.0+dev
// (version is exposed via the gogs `--version` cmdline or the binary metadata, not in ProcessRollup2)
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count latest(Processes.process_path) as process_path values(Processes.user) as gogs_user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("gogs","gogs.exe") by host Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| lookup asset_inventory host OUTPUT gogs_version, internet_facing
| eval major=tonumber(mvindex(split(gogs_version,"."),0))
| eval minor=tonumber(mvindex(split(gogs_version,"."),1))
| eval patch=tonumber(mvindex(split(replace(gogs_version,"\+.*$",""),"."),2))
| where major==0 AND (minor<14 OR (minor==14 AND patch<=2) OR (minor==15 AND like(gogs_version, "%+dev%")))
| sort - internet_facing host
| table host process_path gogs_user gogs_version internet_facing
| tstats summariesonly=false count latest(Processes.process_path) as process_path values(Processes.user) as gogs_user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("gogs","gogs.exe") by host Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

| where major==0 AND (minor<14 OR (minor==14 AND patch<=2) OR (minor==15 AND like(gogs_version, "%+dev%")))

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-39933", "CVE-2024-39932", "CVE-2026-26194", "CVE-2024-39930", "CVE-2025-8110", "CVE-2024-55947")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-39933", "CVE-2024-39932", "CVE-2026-26194", "CVE-2024-39930", "CVE-2025-8110", "CVE-2024-55947")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents

SecurityEvent

AI brands as bait: How threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-06-08 17 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

As threat actors operationalize AI to accelerate attacks, they are also leveraging the wider global interest around AI itself as a social engineering lure. The post AI brands as bait: How threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] ChatGPT Plus payment-update phishing emails (display-name + subject lure) · [LLM] Claude 'Appeal Request' phishing email with PDF attachment lure · [LLM] Phishing redirect chain via awstrack.me / Rebrandly into AI-themed landing path · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — AI brands as bait: How threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering
Installation. Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Connection to AI-brand phishing / installer C2 infrastructure (MSTI June 2026 IOCs) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains

ChatGPT Plus payment-update phishing emails (display-name + subject lure) AIDelivery High
Detects the Microsoft-tracked ChatGPT-themed credential/credit-card phishing wave (4,500 emails to South Africa on 5 May 2026, peaking 100k/day across CH/AT/ZA) that impersonates OpenAI billing with the urgent 'update your payment method or downgrade' lure. Pivots on the verbatim sender display name and subject pattern the campaign uses. Rationale: Pulls the campaign's two strongest invariants: SenderDisplayName 'ChatGPT' and the verbatim Subject token 'ChatGPT Plus' co-occurring with the urgency-lure words ('payment method', 'continues to work', 'downgraded', 'free plan') quoted in the MSTI write-up. Excludes the real openai.com sending domain to drop legitimate billing.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1656
Data sourcesEmail
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (SenderDisplayName =~ "ChatGPT" or SenderFromAddress has "chatgpt")
    and Subject has "ChatGPT Plus"
    and Subject has_any ("payment method","continues to work","update your payment","downgraded","free plan")
| where SenderFromDomain !endswith "openai.com"
| join kind=leftouter (EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderDisplayName, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, Url, UrlDomain, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where OfficeWorkload =~ "Exchange"
| where Subject has "ChatGPT Plus" and Subject has_any ("payment method","continues to work","update your payment","downgraded","free plan")
| where tostring(P2Sender) !endswith "openai.com"
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Subject, Sender = tostring(P2Sender), Recipients = tostring(P2RecipientList), MessageId = tostring(InternetMessageId), Operation
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ChatGPT Plus Payment-Update Phishing Lure
id: 0b1f5e8a-4c5d-4a3b-9b2e-5c1f7a4d8e21
description: Detects MSTI-reported ChatGPT-impersonating phishing wave using the 'update your payment method' urgency lure (May 2026).
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/08/ai-brands-as-bait-how-threat-actors-are-using-the-ai-hype-in-social-engineering/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.t1656
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: threat_management
  category: email
detection:
  selection_subj:
    Subject|contains: 'ChatGPT Plus'
  selection_lure:
    Subject|contains:
      - 'payment method'
      - 'continues to work'
      - 'downgraded'
      - 'free plan'
  filter_legit:
    SenderFromDomain|endswith: 'openai.com'
  condition: selection_subj and selection_lure and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate OpenAI billing notifications (filtered via openai.com)
  - Internal IT communications quoting the lure subject for awareness
level: high
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Email where (Email.src_user_display="ChatGPT*" OR Email.subject="*ChatGPT Plus*") (Email.subject="*payment method*" OR Email.subject="*continues to work*" OR Email.subject="*downgraded*") by Email.src_user, Email.src_user_display, Email.recipient, Email.subject, Email.message_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Email)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Email where (Email.src_user_display="ChatGPT*" OR Email.subject="*ChatGPT Plus*") (Email.subject="*payment method*" OR Email.subject="*continues to work*" OR Email.subject="*downgraded*") by Email.src_user, Email.src_user_display, Email.recipient, Email.subject, Email.message_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Email)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Claude 'Appeal Request' phishing email with PDF attachment lure AIDelivery High
Detects the Anthropic-impersonating phishing wave (20-22 Apr 2026, 2000+ orgs, primarily US/UK/IN tech sector) that uses the display names 'Anthropic Teams' / 'Anthropic PBC', a 'Claude Appeal Request' subject, and a 'Fill and Sign Claude Appeal Form.pdf' attachment carrying the AiTM credential-harvest link to dash.awaydouble[.]org. Rationale: Three article-specific high-fidelity tokens: the verbatim attachment FileName 'Fill and Sign Claude Appeal Form.pdf', the SenderDisplayName values 'Anthropic Teams' / 'Anthropic PBC', and the 'Claude Appeal Request' Subject. The PDF filename alone is essentially zero-FP. The display-name + subject combo is the fallback for renamed attachments. Anti-AiTM lure (dash.awaydouble[.]org) is covered separately in UC3.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1656 T1557
Data sourcesEmail
let suspect_mail = EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SenderDisplayName in~ ("Anthropic Teams","Anthropic PBC")
         or Subject matches regex @"(?i)Claude\s+Appeal\s+Request"
    | where SenderFromDomain !endswith "anthropic.com";
let suspect_attach = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileType =~ "pdf"
    | where FileName =~ "Fill and Sign Claude Appeal Form.pdf"
         or FileName matches regex @"(?i)(Claude|Anthropic).{0,20}Appeal.{0,20}Form.*\.pdf$";
suspect_mail
| join kind=inner suspect_attach on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderDisplayName, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileSize, SHA256, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OfficeWorkload =~ "Exchange"
| where Subject matches regex @"(?i)Claude\s+Appeal\s+Request"
    or tostring(ItemAttachments) has "Fill and Sign Claude Appeal Form.pdf"
| where tostring(P2Sender) !endswith "anthropic.com"
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Subject, Sender = tostring(P2Sender), Recipients = tostring(P2RecipientList), Attachments = tostring(ItemAttachments), MessageId = tostring(InternetMessageId)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Claude Appeal Request Phishing PDF Attachment

Connection to AI-brand phishing / installer C2 infrastructure (MSTI June 2026 IOCs) AICommand & Control High
Network-side detection for the eight Microsoft-published domains backing the ChatGPT/Claude AiTM landing pages and the fake DeepSeek/Manus/Seedance installer C2. Fires on any DNS resolution or HTTP egress to the IOC set; high-fidelity because these are dedicated attacker infrastructure with no known legitimate use. Rationale: Eight domains explicitly attributed by Microsoft Threat Intelligence to this campaign: legendarytrendsbay.shop (ChatGPT phish landing), dash.awaydouble.org / awaydouble.org (Claude AiTM landing), and the four installer-C2 domains. Detection is a literal IOC match — appropriate for alerting tier because attribution is high-confidence and the domains have no legitimate business use.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web
let ioc_domains = dynamic(["legendarytrendsbay.shop","dash.awaydouble.org","awaydouble.org","servicing.pureplantcravings.com","pureplantcravings.com","brokeapt.com","pan.ssffaa19.xyz","ssffaa19.xyz"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend host = tolower(tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host))
| where host in (ioc_domains)
    or RemoteUrl has_any (ioc_domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, host, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let ioc_domains = dynamic(["legendarytrendsbay.shop","dash.awaydouble.org","awaydouble.org","servicing.pureplantcravings.com","pureplantcravings.com","brokeapt.com","pan.ssffaa19.xyz","ssffaa19.xyz"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where tolower(DnsQuery) in (ioc_domains) or DnsQuery has_any (ioc_domains)
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Indicator = DnsQuery, EventVendor, EventProduct, EventKind = "dns"),
    (ImWebSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where Url has_any (ioc_domains) or DstHostname in (ioc_domains)
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Indicator = coalesce(DstHostname, Url), EventVendor, EventProduct, EventKind = "web"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where DestinationHostName has_any (ioc_domains) or RequestURL has_any (ioc_domains)
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname = SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr = SourceIP, SrcUsername = SourceUserName, Indicator = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), EventVendor = DeviceVendor, EventProduct = DeviceProduct, EventKind = "firewall")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Execution or drop of fake AI-platform installer (DeepSeek/Manus/Seedance/GPT-5.5/Kimi) AIInstallation High
Detects the malicious installer binaries Storm-3075 ships through SEO-poisoned GitHub repos masquerading as AI tools (DeepSeek-V4, Manus AI, Seedance, GPT-5.5, Kimi-Swarm). Combines verbatim filename match, the eight MSTI-published SHA256 hashes, and a permissive regex pattern keyed on the consistent '*_x64.exe' naming convention dropped into Downloads/Temp. Rationale: Three layers of fidelity: (1) verbatim FileName match for the seven binaries enumerated in MSTI's lure-table (rows 2-6); (2) hash-equal on all eight published SHA256 IOCs — zero-FP even if the file is renamed; (3) regex on the campaign's consistent '*_x64.exe' naming convention scoped to Downloads/Temp/Public to catch future siblings dropped from the same MSaaS signing pipeline. Article explicitly notes Storm-3075 uses these names through fake GitHub orgs (DeepSeek-V4, ManusAI-agent, bytedance-seedance).
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1608.005 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem

let ai_lure_regex = @"(?i)^(deepseek-v\d+(-pro|-flash)?|manus_ai_desktop|seedance|gpt-\d+(\.\d+)?-(pro|thinking)|kimi-swarm-station)_x64\.exe$";
union isfuzzy=false
    (DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(60d)

        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, EvtKind = "process", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine),

Phishing redirect chain via awstrack.me / Rebrandly into AI-themed landing path AIDelivery Medium
Detects user clicks on the multi-hop redirect chain Storm-3075/affiliates use to launder phish URLs: legit CRM (bitrix24) → Amazon awstrack.me email-tracking → Rebrandly short link → compromised legendarytrendsbay[.]shop /ChatGPT/ path (or sibling AI-themed paths). Targets the SHAPE of the chain (awstrack.me forwarding into an AI-brand path), not just static IOCs, so it also catches campaign rotation. Rationale: Two pivot shapes from the MSTI ChatGPT-phish attack chain: (1) literal IOC match on the six known phish landings; (2) behavioural pattern of a click through awstrack.me/Rebrandly/bitrix24 that terminates at a path containing an AI-brand token — this is the exact funnel diagrammed in Figure 1 and survives URL rotation since the AI-brand path component is the lure invariant. Path-regex /(ChatGPT|Claude|Anthropic|DeepSeek)/ also catches the article's note that the threat actor placed phishing pages in a /ChatGPT/ folder on compromised legendarytrendsbay[.]shop.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1102 T1656
Data sourcesWeb

    or Url matches regex @"(?i)https?://[^/]+/(ChatGPT|Claude|Anthropic|DeepSeek)/"
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlChain, ActionType, IsClickedThrough, IPAddress, Workload
| order by Timestamp desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
