Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution

status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

High

Microsoft's durabletask PyPI Package Compromised in Supply Chain Attack

StepSecurity
2026-06-06 14 use cases 2 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Three malicious versions of Microsoft's official durabletask Python SDK were published to PyPI on May 19, 2026. The compromised package silently downloads and executes a 28 KB payload that steals credentials from AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, password managers, and over 90 developer tool configurations, then spreads laterally through cloud infrastructure. The payload skips systems with a Russian locale, a hallmark of Eastern European cybercrime operations. The attack has been linked to the TeamPCP threat group behind the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Pip install of compromised Microsoft durabletask versions 1.4.1-1.4.3
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Microsoft's durabletask PyPI Package Compromised in Supply Chain Attack
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] rope.pyz dropper executed as /tmp/managed.pyz from durabletask import · [LLM] Fake pgsql-monitor.service systemd persistence written under ~/.config/systemd/user/ · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Egress to TeamPCP rope.pyz C2 infrastructure (check.git-service.com / t.m-kosche.com / 160.119.64.3) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] gh auth token / gpg-decrypt credential harvesting by python3 child · [LLM] Burst of AWS SSM SendCommand / StartSession from stolen durabletask credentials · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Pip install of compromised Microsoft durabletask versions 1.4.1-1.4.3 AIDelivery High
Hunts for pip / python invocations that explicitly request or have resolved to the three trojanized durabletask versions published to PyPI on 19 May 2026. Targets Linux CI runners, build agents, and cloud workloads where the package would be picked up. Rationale: Anchored on the three article-confirmed malicious versions (1.4.1, 1.4.2, 1.4.3) and the publication window of 19 May 2026 16:19 UTC onward. Process telemetry of explicit `pip install durabletask==X.Y.Z` invocations is high-fidelity since the legitimate prior version is 1.4.0 (Apr 8). Tier=alerting because of specific version pins. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1078
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "install"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3") or FileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("durabletask==1.4.1","durabletask==1.4.2","durabletask==1.4.3")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" and ProcessCommandLine !has "durabletask==1.4.0" and ProcessCommandLine !has "durabletask<1.4.1" and Timestamp between (datetime(2026-05-19) .. datetime(2026-05-20T12:00:00Z)))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "install"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("durabletask==1.4.1","durabletask==1.4.2","durabletask==1.4.3")
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine !has "durabletask==1.4.0" and TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-05-19) .. datetime(2026-05-20T12:00:00Z)))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI Versions Installed (TeamPCP)
id: 2f4b8d10-9a52-4d3f-9b21-1e7c6a4f2c11
description: Detects pip installation of the trojanized durabletask versions 1.4.1, 1.4.2, or 1.4.3 published by TeamPCP / Mini Shai-Hulud on 19 May 2026.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/microsofts-durabletask-pypi-package-compromised-in-supply-chain-attack
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:

  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1078
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/pip'
      - '/pip3'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'durabletask==1.4.1'
      - 'durabletask==1.4.2'
      - 'durabletask==1.4.3'
  condition: selection_tool and selection_cmd
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:(*durabletask==1.4.1* OR *durabletask==1.4.2* OR *durabletask==1.4.3*)) AND @process.command_line:*install*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(pip3?|python3?(\.\d+)?)$/i
| regex("durabletask==1\\.4\\.[123]", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("pip","pip3","pip3.10","pip3.11","pip3.12","pip3.13","pip3.14","python","python3") AND (Processes.process="*durabletask==1.4.1*" OR Processes.process="*durabletask==1.4.2*" OR Processes.process="*durabletask==1.4.3*" OR (Processes.process="*install*" AND Processes.process="*durabletask*" AND Processes.process!="*durabletask==1.4.0*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("pip","pip3","pip3.10","pip3.11","pip3.12","pip3.13","pip3.14","python","python3") AND (Processes.process="*durabletask==1.4.1*" OR Processes.process="*durabletask==1.4.2*" OR Processes.process="*durabletask==1.4.3*" OR (Processes.process="*install*" AND Processes.process="*durabletask*" AND Processes.process!="*durabletask==1.4.0*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
rope.pyz dropper executed as /tmp/managed.pyz from durabletask import AIInstallation High
Hunts the unique payload-execution fingerprint from the TeamPCP supply chain attack: a python3 process whose command line references /tmp/managed.pyz, typically spawned via start_new_session=True from a parent python3 -c "import durabletask". Highest-fidelity single signal in the campaign. Rationale: /tmp/managed.pyz is the article-confirmed payload filename the dropper writes via urllib.request.urlretrieve and immediately executes with subprocess.Popen(["python3", "/tmp/managed.pyz"]). The string is unique to this campaign — virtually zero benign use of that exact path. Parent-process pivot on `python3 -c "import durabletask"` adds the chain-of-custody. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1204.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "import durabletask" and FileName in~ ("python","python3"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp asc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or (ParentProcessCommandLine has "import durabletask" and ActingProcessName in~ ("python","python3"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated asc

Egress to TeamPCP rope.pyz C2 infrastructure (check.git-service.com / t.m-kosche.com / 160.119.64.3) AICommand & Control High
Detects DNS lookups or outbound network connections to the article-confirmed C2 domains used to fetch the rope.pyz dropper and to identify the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. Single-hit alerting; these IOCs have no legitimate use. Rationale: Three article-confirmed IOCs with no legitimate use: check.git-service.com (hosts rope.pyz), t.m-kosche.com (secondary attribution beacon tying to TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud), and resolving IP 160.119.64.3 (HostUS / AS7489, AFRINIC). Domain `git-service.com` was registered via NameSilo 16 May 2026 — only 3 days before the attack — so trailing-day FPs are vanishingly unlikely. No external sources cross-checked.

Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web

| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (bad_domains) or RemoteIP == "160.119.64.3"

gh auth token / gpg-decrypt credential harvesting by python3 child AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the rope.pyz collector pattern of harvesting GitHub Personal Access Tokens via gh CLI and GPG-protected secrets via `gpg --batch --passphrase anon --decrypt`, parented by a python3 process — exactly the cmdline strings the article ties to managed.pyz parallel collectors. Rationale: Article-verbatim cmdline strings: `gh auth token`, `gh auth status --show-token`, and `gpg --batch --passphrase anon --decrypt`. The literal passphrase `anon` is an attacker-chosen string with no legitimate use — humans do not use that passphrase for real GPG-protected material. Parented by python3 narrows out interactive developer use of gh. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.005 T1555 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
| where (FileName =~ "gh" and (ProcessCommandLine has "auth token" or ProcessCommandLine has "auth status --show-token"))
   or (FileName =~ "gpg" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("--batch","--passphrase anon","--decrypt"))
| summarize CommandCount = count(),
            Commands = make_set(ProcessCommandLine),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
         by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where CommandCount >= 1
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("python","python3")
| where (ActingProcessName =~ "gh" and (ActingProcessCommandLine has "auth token" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "auth status --show-token"))
   or (ActingProcessName =~ "gpg" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("--batch","--passphrase anon","--decrypt"))
| summarize CommandCount = count(),
            Commands = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
         by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessId, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by FirstSeen desc

Fake pgsql-monitor.service systemd persistence written under ~/.config/systemd/user/ AIInstallation High
Detects creation of the article-named `pgsql-monitor.service` user-level systemd unit file, and the follow-up `systemctl --user daemon-reload` spawned by a python3 process — the exact persistence mechanism each of the four managed.pyz collector instances installs. Rationale: Article names the exact persistence artefact (`pgsql-monitor.service`) and the exact cmdline (`systemctl --user daemon-reload`) spawned by each of the four parallel managed.pyz instances. User-level systemd persistence under `~/.config/systemd/user/` is rare on CI runners and cloud-workload base images. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let file_persist = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where (FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user" and FileName endswith ".service")
     or FileName =~ "pgsql-monitor.service"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="FileWrite";
let daemon_reload = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ "systemctl"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "--user" and ProcessCommandLine has "daemon-reload"
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName="systemctl", FolderPath=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="DaemonReload";
union file_persist, daemon_reload
| order by Timestamp desc
let file_persist = ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified")
  | where (TargetFilePath has "/.config/systemd/user" and TargetFileName endswith ".service")
     or TargetFileName =~ "pgsql-monitor.service"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Signal="FileWrite";
let daemon_reload = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName =~ "systemctl"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--user" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "daemon-reload"
  | where ParentProcessName in~ ("python","python3")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath=ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName="systemctl", ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=ParentProcessCommandLine, Signal="DaemonReload";
union file_persist, daemon_reload
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP pgsql-monitor.service Systemd Persistence (durabletask Compromise)

description: Detects creation of the pgsql-monitor.service user-level systemd unit that rope.pyz installs for persistence, or python3-parented systemctl --user daemon-reload invocations that activate it.

Burst of AWS SSM SendCommand / StartSession from stolen durabletask credentials AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the article's lateral-movement pattern: stolen ~/.aws/credentials being used to enumerate SSM-managed instances and run remote commands or shell sessions. Looks for a single IAM principal calling DescribeInstanceInformation followed by SendCommand or StartSession from a fresh source IP within a short window. Rationale: Article confirms `propagates to other machines through AWS SSM and Kubernetes kubectl exec` after harvesting AWS credentials from ~/.aws/credentials. The high-signal pattern is DescribeInstanceInformation immediately followed by SendCommand or StartSession from the same principal within a short window — classic SSM-as-RCE TTP. Hunting tier because legitimate ops engineers do this too. Defender / Sentinel KQL left empty because their canonical schemas in this tenant do not include AWSCloudTrail; the Sentinel column list above contains no AWSCloudTrail table — operators ingesting CloudTrail via the AWS S3 connector would have a `AWSCloudTrail` table not in the canonical schema. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1078.004 T1580
Data sourcesAuthentication
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:(DescribeInstanceInformation OR SendCommand OR StartSession OR ResumeSession) @evt.outcome:success @userIdentity.type:(IAMUser OR AssumedRole)
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.userName, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName, awsRegion, requestParameters.instanceIds, requestParameters.documentName, requestParameters.target
| filter eventSource = "ssm.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["DescribeInstanceInformation", "SendCommand", "StartSession", "ResumeSession", "GetCommandInvocation"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
| stats count(*) as calls, count_distinct(eventName) as event_types, count_distinct(sourceIPAddress) as src_ips, earliest(@timestamp) as first_seen, latest(@timestamp) as last_seen by userIdentity.arn
| filter event_types >= 2
| sort last_seen desc
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` (eventName=DescribeInstanceInformation OR eventName=SendCommand OR eventName=StartSession OR eventName=ResumeSession) errorCode="*" OR errorCode=NULL
| eval principal=coalesce('userIdentity.arn','userIdentity.userName')
| stats earliest(_time) as firstSeen latest(_time) as lastSeen dc(eventName) as eventTypes values(eventName) as events values(sourceIPAddress) as srcIPs dc(sourceIPAddress) as srcIPCount count by principal
| where eventTypes >= 2 AND srcIPCount >= 1
| eval windowSec=lastSeen-firstSeen
| where windowSec <= 1800
| convert ctime(firstSeen) ctime(lastSeen)
| sort - firstSeen
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

| sort - count

| sort - count

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Bright Data partner-app or brdsdk.framework present on managed iOS / mobile inventory
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Bright Data SDK control-plane beacon to proxyjs/clientsdk endpoints · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Smart-TV / mobile device acting as residential proxy exit node (high-fan-out HTTPS to unrelated public destinations) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Bright Data SDK control-plane beacon to proxyjs/clientsdk endpoints AICommand & Control High
Detects DNS or TLS SNI resolution to the Bright Data residential-proxy SDK control channels (proxyjs/clientsdk on bright-sdk.com, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com). Any endpoint resolving these is either running an app embedding brdsdk.framework or actively relaying scraping jobs as an exit node. Rationale: All five FQDNs (proxyjs.brdtnet.com, proxyjs.luminatinet.com, proxyjs.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.brdtnet.com) are explicitly named in the article body and corroborated by the Include Security research blog as the SDK's exclusive control-plane channel — the article itself recommends blocking them at the router. The article also notes Bright Data's paid commercial service runs on different hosts, so hits here are specifically the embedded-SDK exit-node behaviour. Cross-checked against the Include Security research blog (https://blog.includesecurity.com/2026/06/the-smart-tv-in-your-livingroom-is-a-node-in-the-aiscraping-economy/) which added the broader *.luminati.io SNI pattern and the brdsdk.framework binary identifier. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.includesecurity.com/2026/06/the-smart-tv-in-your-livingroom-is-a-node-in-the-aiscraping-economy/
ATT&CKT1090.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
// Bright Data residential-proxy SDK control-plane beacon
// Endpoints contacting *.bright-sdk.com / *.brdtnet.com / *.luminatinet.com
let brdControlHosts = dynamic(["proxyjs.brdtnet.com","proxyjs.luminatinet.com","proxyjs.bright-sdk.com","clientsdk.bright-sdk.com","clientsdk.brdtnet.com"]);
let brdSuffixes = dynamic([".bright-sdk.com",".brdtnet.com",".luminatinet.com",".luminati.io"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl in~ (brdControlHosts)
    or RemoteUrl has_any (brdSuffixes)
| extend MatchType = case(RemoteUrl in~ (brdControlHosts), "control-plane FQDN",
                          RemoteUrl endswith ".bright-sdk.com", "bright-sdk.com suffix",
                          RemoteUrl endswith ".brdtnet.com", "brdtnet.com suffix",
                          RemoteUrl endswith ".luminatinet.com", "luminatinet.com suffix",
                          RemoteUrl endswith ".luminati.io", "luminati.io suffix",
                          "other")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, MatchType
| order by Timestamp desc
// Bright Data residential-proxy SDK control-plane beacon — ASIM DNS view
let brdControlHosts = dynamic(["proxyjs.brdtnet.com","proxyjs.luminatinet.com","proxyjs.bright-sdk.com","clientsdk.bright-sdk.com","clientsdk.brdtnet.com"]);
let brdSuffixes = dynamic([".bright-sdk.com",".brdtnet.com",".luminatinet.com",".luminati.io"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
  (ImDnsActivity
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where DnsQuery in~ (brdControlHosts)
       or DnsQuery has_any (brdSuffixes)
   | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Indicator = DnsQuery, Source = "ImDnsActivity"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where isnotempty(DestinationHostName)
   | where DestinationHostName in~ (brdControlHosts)
       or DestinationHostName has_any (brdSuffixes)
   | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr = SourceIP, SrcHostname = SourceHostName, SrcUsername = SourceUserName,
             Indicator = DestinationHostName, Source = strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct)),
  (DnsEvents
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where Name has_any (brdSuffixes) or Name in~ (brdControlHosts)
   | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr = ClientIP, SrcHostname = Computer, SrcUsername = "", Indicator = Name, Source = "DnsEvents"))
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count(),
            Indicators = make_set(Indicator, 25), Sources = make_set(Source, 5)
            by SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname
| order by LastSeen desc

Bright Data partner-app or brdsdk.framework present on managed iOS / mobile inventory AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the managed mobile/endpoint fleet for installed apps that ship the Bright Data residential-proxy SDK (brdsdk.framework v1.532.120) — using the article-named partner-app list (Petflix, PlayWorks Digital, CloudTV, Longvision) and Bright Data's published partner page. Catches the exit-node *at install time* rather than waiting for it to phone home. Rationale: Article explicitly names Petflix (Roku), PlayWorks Digital, CloudTV, and Longvision as Bright Data partners shipping the SDK, and identifies brdsdk.framework v1.532.120 as the binary. Include Security additionally surfaced the Swift symbols BrdWebSocketFacade and BrdNetwork.DNSResolver inside the framework. Article notes the partner list is not 1:1 with current SDK inclusion (each app must be verified independently), so this is a hunt not an alert. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.includesecurity.com/2026/06/the-smart-tv-in-your-livingroom-is-a-node-in-the-aiscraping-economy/
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1474.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Software
// Hunt managed fleet for Bright Data SDK partner apps and the brdsdk.framework binary
let brdPartnerApps = dynamic(["Petflix","PlayWorks","CloudTV","Longvision"]);
let brdVendors = dynamic(["PlayWorks Digital","CloudTV","Longvision","Bright Data","Luminati"]);
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareName has_any (brdPartnerApps)
    or SoftwareVendor has_any (brdVendors)
    or SoftwareName contains "brdsdk"
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, OSPlatform, DeviceType, PublicIP, LoggedOnUsers) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, DeviceType, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, PublicIP, LoggedOnUsers, EndOfSupportStatus
| union (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName contains "brdsdk" or FolderPath contains "brdsdk.framework" or FileName has_any ("BrdWebSocketFacade","BrdNetwork")
    | project DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
  )
| order by DeviceName asc

Smart-TV / mobile device acting as residential proxy exit node (high-fan-out HTTPS to unrelated public destinations) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts firewall and NetFlow telemetry for the behavioural signature of a Bright Data exit node: a single internal source (typically an unmanaged smart TV or mobile device) initiates a high volume of outbound HTTPS sessions to many unrelated public web destinations the user is not actively browsing, often during off-hours. The 200 GB/month SDK cap and the device's always-on TV / mobile profile shape the threshold. Rationale: Article quantifies the SDK's monthly traffic ceiling (200 GB/mo, uncapped in some regions) and notes the device 'keeps relaying in the background while someone is watching the screen or on a call, as long as the battery is not low'. The behavioural fingerprint — single internal source, hundreds of unrelated public destinations per hour, outbound bytes ≈ inbound bytes (proxy relay, not browsing) — is what survives even if Bright Data rotates control-plane domains. Article warns 'Bright Data could also change how the SDK connects in the future, which would mean any blocklist needs updating' which is exactly why a behavioural UC complements UC1's IOC UC. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.includesecurity.com/2026/06/the-smart-tv-in-your-livingroom-is-a-node-in-the-aiscraping-economy/
ATT&CKT1090.002 T1496 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
// Managed iOS / mobile exhibiting residential-proxy egress pattern (covers Defender for iOS estate)
let WindowHrs = 1h;
let MinUniqueRemoteIPs = 100;   // residential browsing rarely fans out to >100 distinct public IPs per hour
let MinSessions = 500;          // SDK polling + scraping job throughput floor
let ManagedMobile = DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(24h)
    | where OSPlatform in ("iOS","iPadOS","Android")
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, OSPlatform, DeviceType, PublicIP, LoggedOnUsers) by DeviceId, DeviceName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| join kind=inner ManagedMobile on DeviceId
| summarize UniqueRemoteIPs = dcount(RemoteIP),
            UniqueRemoteUrls = dcount(RemoteUrl),
            Sessions = count(),
            SampleUrls = make_set(RemoteUrl, 25),
            SampleProcess = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, DeviceId, OSPlatform, bin(Timestamp, WindowHrs)
| where UniqueRemoteIPs > MinUniqueRemoteIPs and Sessions > MinSessions
| extend MultiUseSig = iff(UniqueRemoteUrls > 200 and array_length(SampleProcess) <= 2, "likely-proxy", "review")
| order by Sessions desc
// Residential-proxy exit-node behavioural hunt against firewall logs
// Surfaces internal sources fan-out HTTPS to many unrelated public destinations (Bright Data exit-node signature)
let WindowHrs = 1h;
let MinUniqueDests = 250;       // home/IoT devices very rarely exceed this per hour
let MinBytesOut = 524288000;    // 500 MB outbound per hour (200 GB/mo SDK cap → ~280 MB/hr avg, peaks higher)
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DeviceVendor in ("Palo Alto Networks","Fortinet","Cisco","Check Point","Zscaler","SonicWall")
| where DestinationPort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP) == false
| summarize UniqueDestHosts = dcount(DestinationHostName),
            UniqueDestIPs = dcount(DestinationIP),
            BytesOut = sum(toint(SentBytes)),
            BytesIn = sum(toint(ReceivedBytes)),
            Sessions = count(),
            SampleHosts = make_set(DestinationHostName, 25)
            by SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowHrs)
| where UniqueDestHosts > MinUniqueDests and BytesOut > MinBytesOut
| extend GbOut = round(BytesOut / 1073741824.0, 2)
| extend EgressInboundRatio = round(BytesOut * 1.0 / (BytesIn + 1), 2)
| where EgressInboundRatio > 0.4   // proxy traffic: outbound ~= inbound, unlike normal browsing which is inbound-heavy
| order by BytesOut desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true 
    dc(All_Traffic.dest) as uniqueDests

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

CISA Adds Actively Exploited SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Flaw to KEV Catalog

The Hacker News
2026-06-06 10 use cases 6 techniques 4 kill-chain phases detected

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added a high-severity security flaw impacting SolarWinds Serv-U multi-protocol file server software to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-28318 (CVSS score: 7.5), is a denial-of-service (DoS) bug that causes the service to crash

CVEsCVE-2026-28318
ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1486 T1528 T1555.003 T1566

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] SolarWinds Serv-U pre-auth DoS exploit (CVE-2026-28318) — POST with Content-Encoding: deflate · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
SolarWinds Serv-U pre-auth DoS exploit (CVE-2026-28318) — POST with Content-Encoding: deflate AIExploitation High
Detects the specific exploit pattern for CVE-2026-28318: an unauthenticated POST request to a SolarWinds Serv-U file server that carries a Content-Encoding: deflate header, which crashes the Serv-U service. SolarWinds itself recommends blocking any request containing a content-encoding header because the vulnerable service doesn't legitimately use it, making the header presence a high-fidelity signal. Rationale: Article and SolarWinds advisory explicitly call out the trigger: an unauthenticated POST with a Content-Encoding: deflate header crashing Serv-U. The vendor's mitigation guidance — block any request containing a content-encoding header because the vulnerable service doesn't use it — turns header presence into a near-zero-FP signal. Defender query pivots on Serv-U.exe process restarts paired with bursty inbound connections since Defender XDR doesn't natively capture HTTP request headers. Cross-checked against CISA KEV catalog entry and SolarWinds Trust Center advisory wording quoted in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://www.solarwinds.com/trust-center/security-advisories • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-28318
ATT&CKT1499.004 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (21, 22, 80, 443, 990, 8080, 8443)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Serv-U.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "RhinoSoft.Serv-U.exe"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            arg_max(Timestamp, *)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where ConnCount > 50
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "Serv-U.exe" or FileName =~ "RhinoSoft.Serv-U.exe"
    | where ActionType in ("ProcessCreated","ProcessTerminated")
) on DeviceName
| where ProcessCreationTime between (Timestamp - 10m .. Timestamp + 10m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ConnCount, ProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCreationTime
| order by Timestamp desc
// Detect POST requests to Serv-U carrying Content-Encoding header — CVE-2026-28318 pre-auth DoS
// Vendor advisory: header is never legitimately used by Serv-U, so any presence is high-fidelity
let ServUHosts = dynamic(["servu","serv-u","sftp","ftp"]);
let ServUPorts = dynamic([21, 22, 80, 443, 990, 8080, 8443]);
(union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
   | where DestinationPort in (ServUPorts)
   | where Message has "content-encoding" or Message has "Content-Encoding"
            or RequestContext has "content-encoding" or RequestContext has "Content-Encoding"
            or RequestClientApplication has "deflate"
            or DeviceCustomString1 has "content-encoding" or DeviceCustomString2 has "content-encoding"
            or DeviceCustomString3 has "content-encoding" or DeviceCustomString4 has "content-encoding"
            or DeviceCustomString5 has "content-encoding" or DeviceCustomString6 has "content-encoding"
   | extend Host = tolower(DestinationHostName)
   | where Host has_any (ServUHosts) or DestinationServiceName has_any (ServUHosts) or isempty(Host)
   | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort,
             RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct),
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
   | where csMethod =~ "POST"
   | where sSiteName has_any (ServUHosts) or Computer has_any (ServUHosts)
   | project TimeGenerated, cIP, Computer, sSiteName, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, scSubStatus, csUserAgent),
  (Syslog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
   | where ProcessName has_any ("Serv-U","serv-u","servu")
   | where SyslogMessage has "content-encoding" or SyslogMessage has "deflate" or SyslogMessage has "crash" or SyslogMessage has "terminated"
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage))
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SolarWinds Serv-U Pre-Auth DoS via Content-Encoding deflate (CVE-2026-28318)
id: 8c6f3a7e-2d11-4a4b-b9d3-7a3f1e9c4d72
description: Detects POST requests to SolarWinds Serv-U that include a Content-Encoding header — the trigger condition for the CVE-2026-28318 pre-auth DoS. SolarWinds states the vulnerable service does not legitimately use this header.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/cisa-adds-actively-exploited-solarwinds.html
  - https://www.solarwinds.com/trust-center/security-advisories
  - https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/06
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1499.004
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.impact
  - cve.2026.28318
logsource:
  category: webserver
selection:
  cs-method: POST
  cs-host|contains:
    - servu
    - serv-u
  cs-headers|contains:
    - 'content-encoding'

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AI Agent Uncovers 21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg; Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs

The Hacker News
2026-06-06 9 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Two things landed within days of each other this week. A security startup reported 21 previously unknown vulnerabilities in FFmpeg, the media library inside almost everything that touches video, all of them found by an autonomous AI agent. The same week, Google shipped Chrome 149 with patches for 429 security bugs, the most ever in a single release. Only the FFmpeg bugs were found by AI.

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Vulnerable FFmpeg versions exposed to CVE-2026-39210 through CVE-2026-39218 · [LLM] Chrome installs below 149.0.7827.53 carrying CVE-2026-10881 sandbox-escape exposure
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] FFmpeg invoked against untrusted RTSP / AV1-over-RTP sources · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Vulnerable FFmpeg versions exposed to CVE-2026-39210 through CVE-2026-39218 AIWeaponization High
Surfaces managed endpoints carrying FFmpeg builds that fall under the depthfirst-disclosed CVE bundle (CVE-2026-39210..39218) so patch teams can sequence remediation. Targets the SBOM/TVM inventory rather than runtime to catch embedded copies inside Python wheels, container images, and media appliances the article warns about. Rationale: The article enumerates the exact CVE range (CVE-2026-39210 through CVE-2026-39218) assigned to the depthfirst FFmpeg findings and explicitly notes embedded copies inside Python wheels, container images, and appliances are in scope — so the TVM/SBOM angle is the only way to catch the non-system-package variants. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/ai-agent-uncovers-21-zero-days-in.html
ATT&CKT1588.006

FFmpeg invoked against untrusted RTSP / AV1-over-RTP sources AIExploitation Medium
Hunts runtime FFmpeg invocations that ingest the two attack surfaces the article calls out as priority — RTSP and AV1-over-RTP — to identify where pre-patch vulnerable parsers are processing untrusted input. Pre-filters to ffmpeg.exe / ffprobe.exe / ffplay.exe (and the *nix equivalents) with RTSP URIs or AV1-related demuxer/codec flags. Rationale: The article tells defenders to 'prioritize anything that ingests untrusted RTSP or AV1-over-RTP' — those are the specific exposure surfaces tied to the TS demuxer and VP9 decoder bug classes mentioned. Anchoring on ffmpeg/ffprobe/ffplay binaries with rtsp:// URIs, AV1 codec flags, or RTP/MPEG-TS demuxer flags isolates exactly the runtime attack path pre-patch. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/ai-agent-uncovers-21-zero-days-in.html
ATT&CKT1203 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("ffmpeg.exe","ffprobe.exe","ffplay.exe","ffmpeg","ffprobe","ffplay")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("rtsp://","-c:v libdav1d","-c:v av1","libaom-av1","av1_","-f rtp","mpegts")
| extend StreamUrl = extract(@"(?i)(rtsp://[^\s\"]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| extend StreamHost = extract(@"(?i)rtsp://(?:[^@/\s]+@)?([^/:\s]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| extend Av1Flag = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("libdav1d","libaom-av1","av1_","-c:v av1")
| extend RtpFlag = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-f rtp","-f mpegts","-rtsp_transport")
| where StreamUrl != "" or Av1Flag or RtpFlag
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, StreamUrl, StreamHost, Av1Flag, RtpFlag, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("ffmpeg.exe","ffprobe.exe","ffplay.exe","/ffmpeg","/ffprobe","/ffplay")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("rtsp://","-c:v libdav1d","-c:v av1","libaom-av1","av1_","-f rtp","mpegts")
| extend StreamUrl = extract(@"(?i)(rtsp://[^\s\"]+)", 1, TargetProcessCommandLine)
| extend StreamHost = extract(@"(?i)rtsp://(?:[^@/\s]+@)?([^/:\s]+)", 1, TargetProcessCommandLine)
| extend Av1Flag = TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("libdav1d","libaom-av1","av1_","-c:v av1")
| where StreamUrl != "" or Av1Flag
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, StreamUrl, StreamHost, Av1Flag, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FFmpeg Invoked Against Untrusted RTSP or AV1-over-RTP Source
id: 7d2f5b1a-9c4e-4b7a-b3d8-1f0a6e2c8d44
status: experimental
description: Detects FFmpeg family binaries (ffmpeg/ffprobe/ffplay) launched against RTSP URIs or with AV1 / RTP demuxer flags — the two ingestion paths the depthfirst CVE-2026-39210..39218 advisory calls out as priority exposure surfaces.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/ai-agent-uncovers-21-zero-days-in.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/06
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1203
  - cve.2026.39210
  - cve.2026.39211
  - cve.2026.39212
  - cve.2026.39213
  - cve.2026.39214
  - cve.2026.39215
  - cve.2026.39216
  - cve.2026.39217
  - cve.2026.39218
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\ffmpeg.exe'
      - '\ffprobe.exe'
      - '\ffplay.exe'
  selection_cmdline:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'rtsp://'
      - '-c:v libdav1d'
      - '-c:v av1'
      - 'libaom-av1'
      - 'av1_'
      - '-f rtp'
      - '-rtsp_transport'
  condition: selection_image and selection_cmdline
falsepositives:
  - Authorised IP camera / VMS pipelines pulling internal RTSP streams (allowlist their stream hosts)
  - Media transcoding services with documented AV1 jobs
level: medium
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) (@Image:(*\\ffmpeg.exe OR *\\FFmpeg.exe OR *\\ffprobe.exe OR *\\ffplay.exe) OR @process.name:(ffmpeg OR ffprobe OR ffplay)) AND @CommandLine:(*rtsp\:\/\/* OR *libdav1d* OR *libaom-av1* OR *"-c:v av1"* OR *"-f rtp"* OR *"-rtsp_transport"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(ffmpeg|ffprobe|ffplay)\.exe$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/(ffmpeg|ffprobe|ffplay)$/i
| regex("(?i)(rtsp://|libdav1d|libaom-av1|-c:v av1|-f rtp|-rtsp_transport)", field=CommandLine)
| StreamUrl := regex("(?i)(?<stream>rtsp://[^\\s\"]+)", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine, StreamUrl], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("ffmpeg.exe","ffprobe.exe","ffplay.exe","ffmpeg","ffprobe","ffplay")) AND (Processes.process="*rtsp://*" OR Processes.process="*-c:v libdav1d*" OR Processes.process="*-c:v av1*" OR Processes.process="*libaom-av1*" OR Processes.process="*av1_*" OR Processes.process="*-f rtp*" OR Processes.process="*mpegts*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rex field=cmdlines "(?<stream_url>rtsp://[^ \"]+)" | sort - lastSeen
Chrome installs below 149.0.7827.53 carrying CVE-2026-10881 sandbox-escape exposure AIWeaponization High
Surfaces endpoints running Chrome (and Chromium-based browsers re-bundling the same ANGLE component) below the article's fixed build 149.0.7827.53 / .54. CVE-2026-10881 is a CVSS 9.6 OOB read/write in ANGLE that lets a crafted page escape the sandbox and run code on the host, so this is patch-status-as-detection. Rationale: The article names the exact patched Chrome build (149.0.7827.53 Linux / .53-.54 Windows+macOS) and the specific CVE-2026-10881 ANGLE sandbox-escape (CVSS 9.6) — version comparison against that fixed build is the cleanest pre-exploitation visibility. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/ai-agent-uncovers-21-zero-days-in.html
ATT&CKT1189 T1588.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Vulnerabilities
let FixedBuild = "149.0.7827.53";

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where SoftwareVendor in~ ("google","microsoft","brave software","opera") and SoftwareName has_any ("chrome","edge","brave","opera","chromium")
| extend BuildParts = split(SoftwareVersion, ".")
| extend Major = toint(BuildParts[0]), Minor = toint(BuildParts[1]), Patch = toint(BuildParts[2]), Hotfix = toint(BuildParts[3])
| where (SoftwareName has "chrome" and (Major < 149 or (Major == 149 and Patch < 7827) or (Major == 149 and Patch == 7827 and Hotfix < 53)))
   or (SoftwareName has_any ("edge","brave","opera","chromium") and Major < 149)
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | where CveId == "CVE-2026-10881") on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, FixedBuild, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by SoftwareName asc, SoftwareVersion asc
let FixedBuild = "149.0.7827.53";

   or (SoftwareName has "chrome" and VulnerabilitySeverityLevel in ("High","Critical"))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, FixedBuild, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-39210", "CVE-2026-39211", "CVE-2026-39212", "CVE-2026-39213", "CVE-2026-39214", "CVE-2026-39215", "CVE-2026-39216", "CVE-2026-39217", "CVE-2026-39218", "CVE-2026-10881", "CVE-2026-10882", "CVE-2026-10883")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-39210", "CVE-2026-39211", "CVE-2026-39212", "CVE-2026-39213", "CVE-2026-39214", "CVE-2026-39215", "CVE-2026-39216", "CVE-2026-39217", "CVE-2026-39218", "CVE-2026-10881", "CVE-2026-10882", "CVE-2026-10883")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
