Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

Miasma Worm Hits 73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories in Major Supply Chain Attack

The Hacker News
2026-06-06 11 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft's GitHub repositories have become the latest to fall victim to the ongoing Miasma self-replicating supply chain attack campaign. The incident impacted 73 Microsoft repositories across four of its GitHub organizations, including Azure, Azure-Samples, Microsoft, and MicrosoftDocs, per OpenSourceMalware. The development has prompted GitHub to disable access to those repositories. "

GitHub repo created with Miasma/Hades worm signature description AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts for newly-created GitHub repositories whose description matches the Miasma worm's hardcoded tags ('Miasma: The Spreading Blight', spacing variants, and 'Hades - The End for the Damned'). The worm publishes stolen secrets into freshly-minted public repos using these exact descriptions, so a single hit on org-owned identities indicates either an exfil repo from a compromised dev workstation or a hijacked maintainer account. Rationale: The article explicitly enumerates the four exact description strings the worm writes on its exfil repos (13 'Hades' + 82 'Miasma' variants as of writing). Cross-checked with JFrog's 'Miasma: The Spreading Blight Hits Red Hat npm Packages' write-up which confirms the same string convention from May→June 2026. False-positive surface is near-zero — these are not legitimate phrases. Cross-checked against: • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-miasma-redhat-cloud-services/ • https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/mini-shai-hulud-worm-returns-goes-public • https://www.deepwatch.com/labs/ca-26-018-miasma-mini-shai-hulud-compromise-of-red-hat-npm-packages/
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1567
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Requires Defender for Cloud Apps GitHub Enterprise connector
let MiasmaDesc = dynamic(["Miasma: The Spreading Blight","Miasma : The Spreading Blight","Miasma - The Spreading Blight","Hades - The End for the Damned"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("Repository created","Create repository","repo.create","public")
| extend RepoDesc = tostring(RawEventData.description)
| extend RepoName = tostring(RawEventData.repository.name)
| extend ActorLogin = tostring(RawEventData.actor)
| where RepoDesc in~ (MiasmaDesc) or RepoDesc matches regex @"(?i)miasma\s*[: -]\s*the spreading blight" or RepoDesc matches regex @"(?i)hades\s*-\s*the end for the damned"
| project Timestamp, Application, ActorLogin, RepoName, RepoDesc, IPAddress, CountryCode, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// Requires GitHub audit log ingestion (GitHub connector custom table, or CEF→CommonSecurityLog)
let MiasmaRegex = @"(?i)(miasma\s*[: -]\s*the spreading blight|hades\s*-\s*the end for the damned)";
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DeviceVendor has "GitHub" or DeviceProduct has "GitHub"
    | where Activity has_any ("repo.create","public","Repository created")
    | extend RepoDesc = extract(@"description=([^|]+)", 1, Message)
    | where Message matches regex MiasmaRegex or RepoDesc matches regex MiasmaRegex
    | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=DeviceVendor, Actor=SourceUserName, Repo=DestinationServiceName, RepoDesc, SrcIP=SourceIP, Message),
  (OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where OfficeWorkload has "GitHub" and Operation has_any ("repo.create","public")
    | where EventData matches regex MiasmaRegex
    | project TimeGenerated, Vendor="GitHub", Actor=UserId, Repo=ObjectId, RepoDesc=EventData, SrcIP=ClientIP, Message=ResultStatus)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:github (@evt.name:(repo.create OR repo.access OR public) OR @action:(repo.create OR public)) AND (@repository.description:("Miasma: The Spreading Blight" OR "Miasma : The Spreading Blight" OR "Miasma - The Spreading Blight" OR "Hades - The End for the Damned") OR @description:("Miasma: The Spreading Blight" OR "Miasma - The Spreading Blight" OR "Hades - The End for the Damned"))
CLOUD
`github_audit` action="repo.create" OR action="public" OR action="repo.access" 
| eval desc=lower(coalesce(description, repo_description, _raw)) 
| where match(desc, "miasma\s*[:\-]?\s*the spreading blight") OR match(desc, "hades\s*-\s*the end for the damned") 
| stats min(_time) as firstSeen, values(repo) as repos, values(actor) as actors, count by org

AI coding agent spawning Bun runtime — Miasma loader detonation AIInstallation High
Hunts the Miasma worm's primary execution trigger: an AI coding agent process (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code) or `npm test` spawning a `bun` runtime when a developer opens a compromised clone of mantine-datatable / mantine-contextmenu / next-server-actions-parallel. The worm relies on these agents auto-running scripts on workspace open; the parent→child chain agent→bun is highly atypical in normal developer telemetry. Rationale: The article explicitly names the five execution vectors: 'Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code, and the npm test script' (quoted from SafeDep). Parent→child of an IDE/AI-agent process spawning the Bun runtime is otherwise rare; corroborated by JFrog/Akamai IOC tables describing the staged Bun loader as the worm's primary execution stage. Cross-checked against: • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-miasma-redhat-cloud-services/ • https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/mini-shai-hulud-worm-returns-goes-public • https://securityboulevard.com/2026/06/miasma-red-hat-cloud-services-npm-packages-hit-by-a-mini-shai-hulud-style-campaign/

Bun runtime executed from random temp-dir path — Miasma staged loader artifact AIInstallation High
Hunts the Miasma loader's drop location: a `bun` binary executed from a randomized subdirectory under the OS temp tree (`/tmp/b-<random>/bun` on Linux, `/var/folders/.../b-<random>/bun` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\b-<random>\bun.exe` on Windows). The legitimate Bun runtime installs to `~/.bun/bin/bun`, never to a random tempdir subfolder — this folder pattern is a JFrog-confirmed IOC. Rationale: JFrog's IOC bundle explicitly calls out '/tmp/b-<random>/bun on Linux or /var/folders/<...>/b-<random>/bun on macOS' as a high-confidence indicator. The article's '4.3 MB payload runner' + 'staged Bun loader' phrasing matches this drop location. Legitimate Bun installs land under ~/.bun/bin — not under tempdir. Cross-checked against: • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-miasma-redhat-cloud-services/ • https://www.deepwatch.com/labs/ca-26-018-miasma-mini-shai-hulud-compromise-of-red-hat-npm-packages/ • https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/mini-shai-hulud-worm-returns-goes-public

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256

    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Facility == "auth" or ProcessName has "auditd"

Multi-megabyte staged Miasma loader JS dropped to OS temp AIDelivery High
Hunts the worm's staged-loader file artifact: a JavaScript file matching `p<base36>.js` written to `/tmp` (Linux) or `/var/folders` (macOS) by a node/npm/AI-agent parent, with a size >3MB (JFrog measured ~4.1MB; the article cites 4.3MB). Combines the JFrog-confirmed filename pattern with a size floor to discriminate from normal small JS temp files. Rationale: JFrog's IOC table lists '/tmp/p<base36>.js' as the staged loader filename, and the article quotes SafeDep's '4.3 MB payload runner' description. Combining the filename regex with a 3MB size floor cleanly separates this from typical small JS temp files (npm/pnpm/yarn write hundreds of small temps but rarely multi-MB ones into /tmp directly). Cross-checked against: • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-miasma-redhat-cloud-services/ • https://www.deepwatch.com/labs/ca-26-018-miasma-mini-shai-hulud-compromise-of-red-hat-npm-packages/

Bun runtime contacting cloud instance-metadata endpoint — Miasma credential collection AICommand & Control High
Hunts the worm's credential-theft phase: the dropped `bun` process making outbound HTTP requests to AWS/Azure/GCP instance metadata services (IMDS) or to Vault / 1Password / Bitwarden / GitHub-token endpoints. Once detonated, the Miasma stealer queries metadata.google.internal, 169.254.169.254 (AWS), and IMDSv2 / managedidentity.azure.com to lift cloud creds and OIDC tokens. Rationale: JFrog/Akamai/Deepwatch all confirm the Miasma stealer's target list: AWS, Azure, GCP, HashiCorp Vault, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions OIDC, npm, Bitwarden, 1Password. The IMDS endpoints (169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal) are textbook collection paths; combined with a bun parent process from the staged tempdir, FP rate is near-zero. CloudTrail companion query catches the second-stage IMDS token use from the attacker's workstation IP / Bun user-agent. Cross-checked against: • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-miasma-redhat-cloud-services/ • https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/mini-shai-hulud-worm-returns-goes-public • https://panther.com/blog/mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-compromise-of-redhat-cloud-services-npm-packages-via-github-actions-oidc-abuse

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("d630397de8b01af0f6f5cf4463da91b17f28195a2c50c8f3f38ad9f7873fdb8e", "3a9db5ba0c8cd4c91e91717df6b1a141fc1e0fbc0558b5a78d7f5c23f5b2a150", "633c8410ee0413ca4b090a19c30b20c03f31598c25247c484846fa34c1df5b64", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90") or SHA1 in~ ("d630397de8b01af0f6f5cf4463da91b17f28195a2c50c8f3f38ad9f7873fdb8e", "3a9db5ba0c8cd4c91e91717df6b1a141fc1e0fbc0558b5a78d7f5c23f5b2a150", "633c8410ee0413ca4b090a19c30b20c03f31598c25247c484846fa34c1df5b64", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90") or MD5 in~ ("d630397de8b01af0f6f5cf4463da91b17f28195a2c50c8f3f38ad9f7873fdb8e", "3a9db5ba0c8cd4c91e91717df6b1a141fc1e0fbc0558b5a78d7f5c23f5b2a150", "633c8410ee0413ca4b090a19c30b20c03f31598c25247c484846fa34c1df5b64", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("d630397de8b01af0f6f5cf4463da91b17f28195a2c50c8f3f38ad9f7873fdb8e", "3a9db5ba0c8cd4c91e91717df6b1a141fc1e0fbc0558b5a78d7f5c23f5b2a150", "633c8410ee0413ca4b090a19c30b20c03f31598c25247c484846fa34c1df5b64", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90") or SHA1 in~ ("d630397de8b01af0f6f5cf4463da91b17f28195a2c50c8f3f38ad9f7873fdb8e", "3a9db5ba0c8cd4c91e91717df6b1a141fc1e0fbc0558b5a78d7f5c23f5b2a150", "633c8410ee0413ca4b090a19c30b20c03f31598c25247c484846fa34c1df5b64", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90") or MD5 in~ ("d630397de8b01af0f6f5cf4463da91b17f28195a2c50c8f3f38ad9f7873fdb8e", "3a9db5ba0c8cd4c91e91717df6b1a141fc1e0fbc0558b5a78d7f5c23f5b2a150", "633c8410ee0413ca4b090a19c30b20c03f31598c25247c484846fa34c1df5b64", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["d630397de8b01af0f6f5cf4463da91b17f28195a2c50c8f3f38ad9f7873fdb8e", "3a9db5ba0c8cd4c91e91717df6b1a141fc1e0fbc0558b5a78d7f5c23f5b2a150", "633c8410ee0413ca4b090a19c30b20c03f31598c25247c484846fa34c1df5b64", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cisco SD-WAN Manager vconfd_script_upload_*.sh invoked with non-canonical CSV (CVE-2026-20245) AIExploitation High
Hunts for vScript syslog entries on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (vmanage/Validator) showing the vconfd_script_upload_*.sh helpers being invoked with a -cli path argument that points to a file name outside the Cisco-published benign baseline (suffix '_safe.csv'). This is the in-the-wild exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-20245 documented in the Cisco advisory. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim /var/log/scripts.log IOC pattern Cisco published in the advisory: '/usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_*.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv'. The Cisco-supplied benign baseline entries from Jun 5 2026 both end in '_safe.csv' (vsmart_serial_numbers_safe.csv, chassis_numbers_safe.csv), so excluding that suffix isolates the exploit footprint without losing legitimate operator activity. No second-source corroboration available — Cisco's PSIRT advisory and Mandiant's reporting are currently the only sources for the IOC strings.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("vmanage","sdwan","vsmart","validator","manager")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "vconfd_script_upload" and ProcessCommandLine has "-cli path"
| extend ScriptName = extract(@"(vconfd_script_upload_[a-zA-Z_]+\.sh)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| extend CsvPath = extract(@"-cli path (\S+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| where isnotempty(CsvPath)
| where not(CsvPath endswith "_safe.csv") and not(CsvPath startswith "/var/lib/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ScriptName, CsvPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "vconfd_script_upload" and SyslogMessage has "-cli path"
| extend ScriptName = extract(@"(vconfd_script_upload_[a-zA-Z_]+\.sh)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend CsvPath = extract(@"-cli path (\S+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| where isnotempty(CsvPath)
| where not(CsvPath endswith "_safe.csv") and not(CsvPath startswith "/var/lib/")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, ScriptName, CsvPath, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager vconfd Upload Script with Non-Canonical CSV Path (CVE-2026-20245)
id: 7c4d2a5e-1e98-4c1f-b0f1-2c8a47e5d3a2
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-20245 where the vconfd_script_upload_*.sh helpers are invoked with a -cli path argument that does not match the Cisco-published benign baseline (suffix _safe.csv). Mandiant-attributed in-the-wild exploitation produced /var/log/scripts.log entries of this exact shape.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/cisco-catalyst-sd-wan-manager-cve-2026.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/06
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1068
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: syslog
detection:
  selection:
    SyslogMessage|contains|all:
      - 'vconfd_script_upload'
      - '-cli path'
  filter_safe:
    SyslogMessage|contains: '_safe.csv'
  condition: selection and not filter_safe
level: high
source:linux.syslog (@process.name:vScript OR @process.name:vscript) "vconfd_script_upload" "-cli path" -"_safe.csv"
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/vconfd_script_upload/i CommandLine=/-cli path/i
| regex("-cli path (?<CsvPath>\\S+)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT (CsvPath=/_safe\.csv$/i)
| NOT (CsvPath=/^\/var\/lib\//)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CsvPath, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as first_seen from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="*vconfd_script_upload*" AND Processes.process="*-cli path*" by Processes.dest, Processes.process, Processes.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| rex field=process "(?<script_name>vconfd_script_upload_[a-zA-Z_]+\.sh)"
| rex field=process "-cli path (?<csv_path>\S+)"
| where isnotnull(csv_path) AND NOT match(csv_path, "_safe\.csv$") AND NOT match(csv_path, "^/var/lib/")
| sort - first_seen
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as first_seen from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="*vconfd_script_upload*" AND Processes.process="*-cli path*" by Processes.dest, Processes.process, Processes.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| rex field=process "(?<script_name>vconfd_script_upload_[a-zA-Z_]+\.sh)"
| rex field=process "-cli path (?<csv_path>\S+)"
| where isnotnull(csv_path) AND NOT match(csv_path, "_safe\.csv$") AND NOT match(csv_path, "^/var/lib/")
| sort - first_seen
Unauthorized vManage template/config push to SD-WAN edge devices (CVE-2026-20245 impact) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for SD-WAN Manager configuration template pushes to vEdge/cEdge devices initiated by an (actor, source IP) pair never observed pushing in the prior 30 days, or pushed outside the org's change window. Cisco confirmed that CVE-2026-20245 exploitation 'resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices' on victim networks. Rationale: Anchored on Cisco's explicit confirmation that 'exploitation of CVE-2026-20245 resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices'. The detection expresses 'unauthorised change' as a 30-day baseline anti-join over the (actor, source IP) tuple of template-push events, plus an off-hours secondary signal — the cleanest way to surface attacker config pushes on top of vmanage-audit telemetry. Falcon/Defender empty: SD-WAN appliance audit logs do not land in EDR telemetry. CloudWatch empty: not an AWS-native control plane.
ATT&CKT1565.002 T1490 T1485
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
let Lookback = 7d;
let Baseline = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(Lookback))
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("template-push","device-template-attach","config-push")
    | extend ActorUser = extract(@"user[=:](\S+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | extend SrcIp = extract(@"(?:src|client|from)[=:]?\s*(\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | distinct ActorUser, SrcIp;
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("template-push","device-template-attach","config-push")
| extend ActorUser = extract(@"user[=:](\S+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend SrcIp = extract(@"(?:src|client|from)[=:]?\s*(\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend TargetTemplate = extract(@"template[=:](\S+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend PushHour = hourofday(TimeGenerated)
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on ActorUser, SrcIp
| summarize FirstPush=min(TimeGenerated), Pushes=count(), Templates=make_set(TargetTemplate, 50), OffHourPushes=countif(PushHour < 6 or PushHour > 20) by ActorUser, SrcIp, Computer
| order by FirstPush desc
source:linux.syslog ("template-push" OR "device-template-attach" OR "config-push") ("vmanage-audit" OR @process.name:vmanage*)
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as first_push values(All_Changes.object) as targets from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.action IN ("template-push","device-template-attach","config-push") AND All_Changes.object_category="network" by All_Changes.user, All_Changes.src, All_Changes.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)`
| eval push_hour=tonumber(strftime(first_push,"%H"))
| lookup change_window_lookup user OUTPUT change_window_user
| where isnull(change_window_user) OR (push_hour<6 OR push_hour>20)
| sort - first_push
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as first_push values(All_Changes.object) as targets from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.action IN ("template-push","device-template-attach","config-push") AND All_Changes.object_category="network" by All_Changes.user, All_Changes.src, All_Changes.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)`
| eval push_hour=tonumber(strftime(first_push,"%H"))
| lookup change_window_lookup user OUTPUT change_window_user
| where isnull(change_window_user) OR (push_hour<6 OR push_hour>20)
| sort - first_push
Cisco vManage auth-bypass exploitation chained into CVE-2026-20245 (CVE-2026-20182 / CVE-2026-20127) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for the authentication-bypass primitive the attacker uses to obtain netadmin before chaining CVE-2026-20245. Looks for external IPs probing vManage admin/API endpoints (/dataservice/, /j_security_check, /admin/) followed within 5 minutes by an authenticated netadmin session from the same source — the pattern Cisco implicates for the chained exploit. Rationale: Built around the article's statement that CVE-2026-20245 requires netadmin obtained 'through valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127' — both pre-auth bypasses against the same vManage management plane. /j_security_check and /dataservice/ are the historical vManage entry points abused in Cisco's prior advisories for similar auth-bypass CVEs, so the correlation of external probing → netadmin login from the same source within 5m is the high-fidelity chain signal. Falcon/Defender empty: vManage web traffic does not land in EDR telemetry. CloudWatch empty: not AWS-native.
ATT&CKT1190 T1078 T1212
Data sourcesWeb.Web Authentication.Authentication
let SuspectAccess = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DeviceProduct has_any ("vManage","SD-WAN","Catalyst") or DestinationServiceName has "vmanage"
    | where RequestURL has_any ("/j_security_check","/dataservice/","/admin/")
    | where not(ipv4_is_private(SourceIP))
    | summarize ReqCount=count(), Paths=dcount(RequestURL), Statuses=make_set(EventOutcome, 10), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName
    | where ReqCount > 5 and Paths > 1;
let Logins = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("login success","netadmin","admin logged in","AAA login")
    | extend LoginUser = extract(@"user[=:](\S+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | extend LoginSrcIp = extract(@"(?:src|client|from)[=:]?\s*(\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | where isnotempty(LoginSrcIp)
    | project LoginTime=TimeGenerated, LoginUser, LoginSrcIp;
SuspectAccess
| join kind=inner Logins on $left.SourceIP == $right.LoginSrcIp
| where LoginTime between (FirstSeen .. (LastSeen + 5m))

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07

tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:

            - '\wscript.exe'

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"

HTTP access to Shopper admin team-settings / Livewire endpoints (CVE-2026-47744) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts HTTP requests to the vulnerable Shopper admin panel routes — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — including their Livewire AJAX endpoints. Pre-patch (Shopper < 2.8.0) these were reachable by any authenticated panel user and were the only network observable for the authorization-bypass / RBAC privilege-escalation chain disclosed in GHSA-c3qp-2ggw-xjg7. Rationale: The article names exactly two Livewire components — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — as the abuse surface. Livewire routes those component names verbatim through /livewire/update (Livewire v3) and /livewire/message/{component} (v2), so the component string and these endpoints are the highest-fidelity strings available pre-exploit. POST/PUT/PATCH on the role-permission route is the specific action that grants/escalates permissions, distinguishing exploitation from normal page loads. No external IOC corroboration was attempted since the advisory exposes no network IOCs — only source-code paths.
ATT&CKT1190 T1068 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Requires IIS / nginx access logs ingested to a custom table; M365 Defender XDR does not natively capture inbound HTTP to a self-hosted PHP app.
// Pivot via DeviceNetworkEvents for the web server's inbound traffic to the panel's listening port, then triage in the proxy/WAF.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where LocalPort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm.exe","php.exe","nginx.exe","httpd.exe","caddy.exe")
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| summarize Connections = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where Connections > 5
| order by LastSeen desc
let TargetPaths = dynamic(["settings/team","settings.team.index","settings.team.role-permission","settings.team.rolepermission","/livewire/update","/livewire/message/settings.team"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where csUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or csUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Computer, Method=csMethod, Url=strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Status=scStatus, ClientIP=cIP, UserAgent=csUserAgent, User=csUserName),
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where CsUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or CsUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="AppService", Computer=CsHost, Method=CsMethod, Url=strcat(CsUriStem, iff(isnotempty(CsUriQuery), strcat("?", CsUriQuery), "")), Status=ScStatus, ClientIP=CIp, UserAgent=UserAgent, User=CsUsername),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where RequestURL has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source=DeviceProduct, Computer=DestinationHostName, Method=RequestMethod, Url=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), ClientIP=SourceIP, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, User=SourceUserName)
)
| where Method in~ ("POST","PUT","PATCH") or Url has_any ("role-permission","rolepermission")
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Methods = make_set(Method), Statuses = make_set(Status), UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 5), Users = make_set(User, 10) by ClientIP, Computer, Source
| order by LastSeen desc

Unauthenticated POST to AIT-BSC /<name>/start with path-traversal form fields (CVE-2026-47731) AIExploitation High
Hunts the actual exploit shape against the AIT-Core BSC HTTP API: POST to /<name>/start carrying attacker-controlled log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, or path form fields with path-traversal indicators (../, %2e%2e, absolute paths like /etc, /home, /root). Pre-patch AIT-Core <3.1.1 and <2.6.1 lets an unauthenticated remote caller use these fields to redirect log_file writes anywhere ait-bsc can write — corruption of .py modules then yields RCE on next restart. Rationale: Targets the exact REST shape from the article (the Bottle route `/<name>/start` registered in `StreamCaptureManagerServer._route()`) plus the three attacker-influenced form fields named in the bug write-up (log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, path) combined with traversal markers (../ %2e%2e absolute /etc /root /home). The article confirms there is no auth on the route and these fields go straight into `os.path.join` without realpath canonicalisation. Cross-checked against the GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 advisory and the AIT-Core 3.1.1/2.6.1 patch notes which scope the same parameter list. Falcon FDR doesn't natively ship HTTP request bodies so falcon_logscale_query is empty; the same telemetry is covered by NetworkConnectIP4 in UC2. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/releases/tag/3.1.1
ATT&CKT1190 T1565.001

| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(python(3(\.\d+)?)?|ait-bsc)(\.exe)?$"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ait-bsc","ait.core.bsc","ait_bsc","StreamCaptureManagerServer","bsc.yaml")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Sessions=count(), AnyLocalPort=any(LocalPort) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let TraversalTokens = dynamic(["log_dir_path","file_name_pattern","..%2F","..%2f","..%5C","..%5c","%2e%2e","path=%2F","path=/etc","path=/root","path=/home","path=/var","path=/tmp","log_dir_path=/"]);
let IISHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)^/[^/]+/start$"
    | where csUriQuery has_any (TraversalTokens) or csUriStem has_any ("%2e%2e", "..")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=tostring(cIP), DstPort=tostring(sPort), Uri=csUriStem, Detail=csUriQuery, UA=csUserAgent, Source="W3CIIS";
let CEFHits = CommonSecurityLog

ait-bsc outbound TCP to public/non-baseline destination (attacker-supplied loc port) AICommand & Control High
Detects ait-bsc / python processes running the ait.core.bsc StreamCaptureManager opening outbound TCP/UDP sessions to non-RFC1918, non-baseline destinations. Per CVE-2026-47731 the unauth /<name>/start endpoint lets a remote caller supply arbitrary `loc` + `port` form values which BSC dutifully `gevent.spawn`s a socket against — making BSC initiate egress to attacker-controlled infrastructure that then streams attacker-chosen bytes back into the file append sink. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article-confirmed primitive: the attacker controls `loc` and `port` in the form body and BSC `gevent.spawn`s a SocketStreamCapturer at that endpoint — i.e. BSC initiates the egress under attacker direction. Process-context match uses the exact module path (`ait.core.bsc`), class name (`StreamCaptureManagerServer`), and config file (`bsc.yaml`) shown in the source excerpt. Sentinel query splits process-context resolution onto ImProcessCreate (which carries ActingProcessCommandLine) and joins by DvcHostname into ImNetworkSession (which does not) — the schema-correct way to express the same logic the Defender query expresses inline. Cross-checked against GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 patch diff which restricts socket creation to validated paths only. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/blob/main/ait/core/bsc.py

Installation of compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI versions 1.4.1-1.4.3 AIDelivery High
Detects pip installation of the three malicious durabletask SDK versions (1.4.1, 1.4.2, 1.4.3) published to PyPI on 2026-05-19. Hits every CI runner, build host, or developer workstation that pulled the trojanised release; pin to 1.4.0 and treat any match as compromised. Rationale: Pins on the three article-named malicious versions of the official 400k-DL/month durabletask package, only legitimate channel is pip install referencing one of those version strings. Hashes (069ac1dc... / 7d80b3ef... / aeaf583e...) cross-referenced via StepSecurity public run analysis. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python3","python3.14","python")
   or FileName in~ ("pip","pip3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousVersions = dynamic(["1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python3","python3.14","python")
   or TargetProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (MaliciousVersions) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (MaliciousVersions)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Python urlretrieve download of rope.pyz from check.git-service.com to /tmp/managed.pyz AIInstallation High
Catches the 14-line dropper executing at `import durabletask` time: a Python process performs an HTTPS GET to check.git-service.com/rope.pyz and writes the response to /tmp/managed.pyz. Highly specific to the TeamPCP rope.pyz framework — the URL path /rope.pyz and target filename /tmp/managed.pyz are both attacker-chosen literals. Rationale: Three article-grounded literals correlated: process is python*, destination is `check.git-service.com` (or its 160.119.64.3 / 83.142.209.194 IPs), and the write target is `/tmp/managed.pyz`. Any pair is suspicious; all three is the dropper. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.006
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Filesystem
let TimeRange = ago(30d);
let C2 = dynamic(["check.git-service.com","git-service.com"]);
let C2IP = dynamic(["160.119.64.3","83.142.209.194"]);
let Net = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > TimeRange
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (C2) or RemoteIP in (C2IP);
let Drop = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > TimeRange
    | where FolderPath == "/tmp" and FileName =~ "managed.pyz"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14");
union Net, Drop
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let TimeRange = ago(30d);
let C2 = dynamic(["check.git-service.com","git-service.com"]);
let C2IP = dynamic(["160.119.64.3","83.142.209.194"]);
let Net = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
    | where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("Python-urllib","python-requests","python3")
         or Url has "rope.pyz"
    | where HttpHostName has_any (C2) or DstIpAddr in (C2IP) or Url has_any (C2)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, HttpHostName, Url, DstIpAddr;
let Drop = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
    | where TargetFilePath has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath;
union Net, Drop
| order by TimeGenerated desc

python3 import durabletask spawning detached /tmp/managed.pyz collector swarm AIInstallation High
Detects the rope.pyz post-import behaviour: a single `python3 -c "import durabletask"` parent spawning multiple `python3 /tmp/managed.pyz` children, each detached via start_new_session=True. Hunting for the parent→child binary pair `/tmp/managed.pyz` is essentially zero-FP — that path was attacker-chosen specifically to look bland. Rationale: Article explicitly enumerates the process tree: PID 2380/2404/2430/2432 all `python3 /tmp/managed.pyz` from a single parent. The cmdline literal `/tmp/managed.pyz` + python parent is article-specific and not a generic LOLBin pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485

| order by FirstSeen desc

Fake pgsql-monitor.service persistence via systemctl --user daemon-reload from python parent AIInstallation High
rope.pyz installs a fake systemd user unit named pgsql-monitor.service then issues `systemctl --user daemon-reload`. Detects the cmdline `systemctl --user daemon-reload` when spawned by python3 — and any creation of a unit file named pgsql-monitor.service. Non-obvious persistence path: user-scope (not system) so root isn't needed. Rationale: Two article-specific literals: the deliberately bland service name `pgsql-monitor.service` and the `systemctl --user daemon-reload` cmdline spawned by python3. Neither is a normal admin operation in a CI runner or microservice host. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485

GPG batch passphrase 'anon' + gh auth token credential harvesting from python parent AIActions on Objectives High
rope.pyz collectors invoke `gpg --batch --passphrase anon --decrypt` (a literal, hard-coded passphrase) and `gh auth token` / `gh auth status --show-token` from a python3 parent. The cmdline `--passphrase anon` is essentially unique to this campaign; `gh auth token` from a non-shell parent (python3) is the second high-fidelity tell. Rationale: `--passphrase anon` is a literal attacker-chosen passphrase essentially unique to rope.pyz; `gh auth token` parented by python3 is unusual everywhere (gh is interactive CLI). Article enumerates both for every managed.pyz child. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485

id: 6b1f2a18-3d44-4f10-93c6-7f3a9b8e1f05
description: Detects the rope.pyz credential collectors invoking gpg --batch --passphrase anon --decrypt and gh auth token/status --show-token from a python3 parent.
references:

logsource:
  category: process_creation

detection:
  parent_python:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/python3.14'
  gpg_anon:
    Image|endswith: '/gpg'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '--batch'
      - '--passphrase anon'
      - '--decrypt'
  gh_token:
    Image|endswith: '/gh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'auth token'
      - 'auth status --show-token'
  condition: parent_python and (gpg_anon or gh_token)
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) @process.parent.name:(python OR python3 OR python3.14) ((@process.name:gpg @process.command_line:(*--batch* *--passphrase\ anon* *--decrypt*)) OR (@process.name:gh @process.command_line:(*"auth token"* OR *"auth status --show-token"*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(python3?(\.14)?)$/i
| (ImageFileName=/\/gpg$/i AND regex("--batch.*--passphrase\\s+anon.*--decrypt", field=CommandLine))
  OR (ImageFileName=/\/gh$/i AND regex("auth\\s+(token|status\\s+--show-token)", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
